100 #: id is a fingerprint of THESE, not of the last commit.
101 _BUILD_SOURCES = (
102     "anchor_gui.py", "route_table.py", "chamber_open.py", "chamber_rail.py",
103     "chamber_page.py", "chamber_efforts.py", "chamber_status_overlay.py",

109 # id, so open cockpit pages never self-healed (the exact 2026-08-15 class, re-opened on
110 # the new primary surface). The cockpit tree now counts.
111 _BUILD_SOURCE_GLOBS = (
112     "static/*.js", "static/*.css", "static/*.html",
113     "steward_cockpit/*.py", "steward_cockpit/static/*.js",

118 def _compute_build_id():
119     """A build id that changes when the CODE ON DISK changes.
120 
121     (2026-08-15, John: "You have promised me so many times that updated code is
122     available once I restart and it is not there… how can we get this fixed for
123     good?")
124 
125     THE BUG THIS FIXES. This was `git rev-parse --short HEAD`. BUILD_ID feeds
126     three things: the asset `?v=` cache-buster, `window.__ANCHOR_BUILD__`, and
127     `GET /api/version` — which the page polls every 30s and RELOADS ITSELF when
128     the value changes. Keyed on HEAD, all three froze for any work that was not
129     yet committed. So on a tree with uncommitted changes: the server restarts
130     with new code, reports the SAME version, the self-healing reload never
131     fires, an open page keeps showing the old render, and the honest report
132     "I restarted and nothing changed" is met with "try refreshing" — which
133     cannot help, because the page was never told there was anything new.
134 
135     A whole day of edits shipped under one unchanging id this way.
136 
137     Now: git HEAD stays as the readable prefix (it says which commit the tree is
138     based on) and a fingerprint of the served sources' size+mtime is appended,
139     so ANY edit — committed or not — moves the id. Cheap (a few dozen stat()
140     calls, once, at import), and it never raises.
141     """
142     import subprocess
143     head = ""
144     try:
145         out = subprocess.run(
146             ["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"],
147             cwd=str(ANCHOR_DIR),
148             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
149             creationflags=_paths.NO_WINDOW,
150         )
151         if out.returncode == 0:
152             head = (out.stdout or "").strip()
153     except Exception:
154         head = ""
155 
156     stamps = []
157     try:
158         import glob as _glob
159         paths = [ANCHOR_DIR / name for name in _BUILD_SOURCES]
160         for pattern in _BUILD_SOURCE_GLOBS:
161             paths.extend(Path(p) for p in _glob.glob(str(ANCHOR_DIR / pattern)))
162         for p in sorted(paths, key=str):
163             try:
164                 st = p.stat()
165                 # 2026-08-25 hardening: RELATIVE PATH (basenames alias across the
166                 # cockpit/static dirs) + ns mtime (int seconds missed fast edits).
167                 try:
168                     rel = str(p.relative_to(ANCHOR_DIR))
169                 except ValueError:
170                     rel = str(p)
171                 stamps.append("%s:%d:%d" % (rel, st.st_size, st.st_mtime_ns))
172             except OSError:
173                 continue
174     except Exception:
175         stamps = []
176 
177     if stamps:
178         digest = hashlib.sha1("|".join(stamps).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:7]
179         return ("%s+%s" % (head, digest)) if head else digest
180     if head:
181         return head
182     try:
183         return str(int(os.path.getmtime(__file__)))
184     except Exception:
185         return "0"
186

192 # Self-healing cache-bust client JS. Kept as a plain (non-f) string so it can
193 # be embedded verbatim in BOTH the f-string dashboard page (generate_html) and
194 # the concatenated project-window page without brace-doubling concerns. The
195 # build id is substituted via a simple placeholder, not f-string formatting.
196 _CACHE_BUST_JS_TEMPLATE = """
197 (function () {
198   try {
199     window.__ANCHOR_BUILD__ = "__ANCHOR_BUILD_ID__";
200     // Kill any leftover service worker registered by an OLD Anchor build.
201     if (navigator.serviceWorker && navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations) {
202       navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations().then(function (rs) {
203         rs.forEach(function (r) { try { r.unregister(); } catch (e) {} });
204       }).catch(function () {});
205     }
206     // Best-effort: clear any stale Cache Storage entries.
207     if (window.caches && caches.keys) {
208       caches.keys().then(function (ks) {
209         ks.forEach(function (k) { try { caches.delete(k); } catch (e) {} });
210       }).catch(function () {});
211     }
212     // (2026-09-04, John) "the cockpit refreshed on its own ... and cleared the
213     // dialogue while I was typing" — that was THIS reload, fired by a redeploy.
214     // Two rules now: (1) never reload while a text field has focus or holds
215     // unsent text — wait for the next check; (2) before any reload, stash every
216     // draft (textareas + text inputs) in sessionStorage and put it back after.
217     var DRAFT_KEY = 'anchor_drafts:' + location.pathname;
218     function draftFields() {
219       var out = [];
220       var els = document.querySelectorAll('textarea, input[type=text], input[type=search], input:not([type])');
221       for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) out.push(els[i]);
222       return out;
223     }
224     function fieldKey(el, i) {
225       return (el.getAttribute('data-say') != null ? 'data-say' : (el.id || el.name || '')) + '#' + i;
226     }
227     function typing() {
228       var a = document.activeElement;
229       if (a && (a.tagName === 'TEXTAREA' || a.tagName === 'INPUT') && (a.value || '').length) return true;
230       var els = draftFields();
231       for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) if ((els[i].value || '').trim().length) return true;
232       return false;
233     }
234     function stashDrafts() {
235       try {
236         var els = draftFields(), d = [];
237         for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) if ((els[i].value || '').length) d.push({ k: fieldKey(els[i], i), v: els[i].value });
238         if (d.length) sessionStorage.setItem(DRAFT_KEY, JSON.stringify(d)); else sessionStorage.removeItem(DRAFT_KEY);
239       } catch (e) {}
240     }
241     function restoreDrafts() {
242       try {
243         var raw = sessionStorage.getItem(DRAFT_KEY);
244         if (!raw) return;
245         sessionStorage.removeItem(DRAFT_KEY);
246         var d = JSON.parse(raw), els = draftFields(), byKey = {};
247         for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) byKey[fieldKey(els[i], i)] = els[i];
248         for (var j = 0; j < d.length; j++) {
249           var el = byKey[d[j].k];
250           if (el && !(el.value || '').length) { el.value = d[j].v; try { el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true })); } catch (e) {} }
251         }
252       } catch (e) {}
253     }
254     function checkVersion() {
255       fetch('/api/version', { cache: 'no-store' })
256         .then(function (r) { return r.json(); })
257         .then(function (d) {
258           var v = d && d.version;
259           if (!v || v === window.__ANCHOR_BUILD__) return;
260           if (typing()) return; // his words outrank a redeploy; try again next check
261           // Loop guard: never reload more than once per server version.
262           var key = 'anchor_reloaded_for';
263           try {
264             if (sessionStorage.getItem(key) === String(v)) return;
265             sessionStorage.setItem(key, String(v));
266           } catch (e) {}
267           stashDrafts();
268           location.replace(location.pathname + '?v=' + encodeURIComponent(v));
269         })
270         .catch(function () {});
271     }
272     if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', restoreDrafts);
273     else restoreDrafts();
274     setTimeout(restoreDrafts, 1500); // pages that build their fields after load
275     checkVersion();
276     setInterval(checkVersion, 30000);
277   } catch (e) {}
278 })();
279 """

292 # ── Contract-versioning shim (re-architecture 2026-07 · W2) ─────────────────
293 # ``window.ANCHOR_BOOT`` is the VERSIONED server→client bootstrap channel.
294 # W2 ships it minimally — the build id + the auth flag — as the deploy-safety
295 # contract shim (the LAST pre-migration release): every ``_postJson`` declares
296 # the page's build id via the ``X-Anchor-Build`` header, and a mismatch is
297 # answered with a STRUCTURED 409 the stale client renders as a 'reload
298 # required' banner (stale-tab / PWA-cached iPad client protection). W4 grows
299 # ANCHOR_BOOT into the ONLY server→client state channel for the extracted
300 # static frontend (token presence, project id, feature flags, initial counts).
301 ANCHOR_BOOT_SCHEMA_VER = 1
302 
303 #: The structured 409 discriminator the client JS matches on. Keep stable —
304 #: old clients in the field match this exact string forever.
305 BUILD_MISMATCH_ERROR = "build-mismatch"

308 def anchor_boot(extra=None):
309     """Assemble the ``window.ANCHOR_BOOT`` bootstrap dict.
310 
311     Documented contract (versioned via ``schema_ver``; additive-only):
312       - ``schema_ver``     — int, the ANCHOR_BOOT shape version;
313       - ``build_id``       — the server build this page was rendered from;
314       - ``auth_required``  — whether the server has ANCHOR_TOKEN configured
315                              (token PRESENCE only — never the value).
316     ``extra`` lets a render surface add page-scoped keys. Never embeds the
317     token VALUE itself — only its presence.
318 
319     W4 (static frontend, rearch C1 increment 1) — the PROJECT WINDOW adds,
320     via ``extra`` = :func:`project_window_boot_extra`:
321       - ``page``                   — ``"project-window"``;
322       - ``project_id``             — the window's project id;
323       - ``grass_dev_label_prefix`` — ``effort_history.GRASS_DEV_LABEL_PREFIX``
324                                      (the [grass-dev] top-strip filter marker);
325       - ``flags``                  — feature flags (``{"frontend": "static"}``);
326       - ``counts``                 — initial counts (``sessions`` /
327                                      ``live_sessions`` from the managed-session
328                                      registry; best-effort zeros on error).
329     On the static-frontend path this dict is the ONLY server→client state
330     channel for the project window: the page derives its legacy globals from
331     it client-side (``_PW_BOOT_GLOBALS_JS``) and the app JS arrives as a
332     static file — no other per-page server value injection exists.
333     """
334     boot = {
335         "schema_ver": ANCHOR_BOOT_SCHEMA_VER,
336         "build_id": BUILD_ID,
337         "auth_required": bool(_paths.expected_token()),
338     }
339     if extra:
340         boot.update(extra)
341     return boot

364 def _read_md_text(filepath):
365     """Read a markdown file as text, resilient to non-UTF-8 bytes.
366 
367     Anchor always writes markdown as UTF-8, but a file edited by an external
368     tool can arrive in another encoding (e.g. a Windows-1252 em-dash, byte
369     0x97). A single such byte must never take down the dashboard: try strict
370     UTF-8 first, and on a UnicodeDecodeError fall back to a lenient decode so
371     the stray byte degrades to a replacement char instead of raising. The next
372     write re-saves the file as clean UTF-8. The daily healthcheck still reads
373     strictly, so a malformed file is still surfaced there for cleanup.
374     """
375     try:
376         return filepath.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
377     except UnicodeDecodeError:
378         return filepath.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

399 def gather_all():
400     """Read everything from both directories, return (projects, tasks, inbox)."""
401     all_tasks = []
402     seen = set()
403 
404     def _add(task_list, default_domain=None):
405         for t in task_list:
406             key = t["text"].lower().strip()[:60]
407             if key not in seen:
408                 seen.add(key)
409                 if default_domain and t["domain"] == "personal":
410                     t["domain"] = default_domain
411                 all_tasks.append(t)
412 
413     # Collect per-render warnings locally; a single unreadable/unparseable file
414     # must be skipped (recorded here) rather than 500-ing the whole dashboard.
415     # We accumulate into a local list and publish it atomically at the end, so
416     # concurrent gather_all() calls (ThreadingHTTPServer) never observe a torn
417     # mid-clear state of the module global.
418     _warn = []
419 
420     def _safe(parse_fn, src, *, into, **kw):
421         try:
422             into(parse_fn(src), **kw)
423         except Exception as e:  # one bad file can't take down every view
424             _warn.append(f"{getattr(src, 'name', src)}: {e}")
425 
426     if DASHBOARD_MD.exists():
427         _safe(parse_tasks_from_md, DASHBOARD_MD, into=_add)
428     if DOMAINS_DIR.exists():
429         for f in sorted(DOMAINS_DIR.glob("*.md")):
430             _safe(parse_tasks_from_md, f, into=_add, default_domain=f.stem)
431 
432     projects = []
433     seen_p = set()
434     if PROJECTS_MD.exists():
435         try:
436             parsed_projects = parse_projects_from_md(PROJECTS_MD)
437         except Exception as e:
438             parsed_projects = []
439             _warn.append(f"{PROJECTS_MD.name}: {e}")
440         for p in parsed_projects:
441             key = p["name"].lower().strip()[:60]
442             if key not in seen_p:
443                 seen_p.add(key)
444                 projects.append(p)
445 
446     inbox = []
447     if INBOX_MD.exists():
448         try:
449             inbox.extend(parse_inbox_from_md(INBOX_MD))
450         except Exception as e:
451             _warn.append(f"{INBOX_MD.name}: {e}")
452 
453     # Publish warnings atomically (slice-assign in place, no clear/append window).
454     LAST_GATHER_WARNINGS[:] = _warn
455 
456     # Filter out synthetic health-check probes so they never appear in any view
457     all_tasks = [t for t in all_tasks if "__healthcheck__" not in t["text"].lower()]
458     inbox = [i for i in inbox if "__healthcheck__" not in i["text"].lower()]
459 
460     return projects, all_tasks, inbox
461

468 def latest_health_report():
469     """Return (date_str, status, path) for the most recent health report, or None.
470 
471     status is "OK" or "ISSUES FOUND" (taken from the second non-blank line of the report).
472     """
473     if not HEALTH_REPORTS_DIR or not HEALTH_REPORTS_DIR.exists():
474         return None
475     reports = sorted(HEALTH_REPORTS_DIR.glob("*.md"), reverse=True)
476     for r in reports:
477         if r.name.lower() == "readme.md":
478             continue
479         try:
480             text = r.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
481         except Exception:
482             continue
483         m = re.search(r'^Status:\s*(.+)$', text, re.MULTILINE)
484         if m:
485             status = m.group(1).strip()
486             return (r.stem, status, r)
487     return None
488

496     return files

540 # ── Hand-rolled stdlib WebSocket frame codec (RFC 6455) — PURE functions ─────
541 # v3 "Mission Control" (MASTER-PLAN §D / Wave 3). The ConPTY terminal transport
542 # is a minimal hand-rolled WebSocket carrying PTY bytes both ways over the raw
543 # socket. The frame codec is factored into PURE, socket-free functions so it is
544 # unit-testable without a connection.
545 import base64 as _b64
546 import hashlib as _hashlib
547 import struct as _struct
548 
549 #: The RFC 6455 GUID concatenated with the client key to derive the accept hash.
550 WS_GUID = "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11"
551 
552 # WebSocket opcodes.
553 WS_OP_CONT = 0x0
554 WS_OP_TEXT = 0x1
555 WS_OP_BINARY = 0x2
556 WS_OP_CLOSE = 0x8
557 WS_OP_PING = 0x9
558 WS_OP_PONG = 0xA
559 
560 
561 def ws_accept_key(client_key: str) -> str:
562     """Compute the ``Sec-WebSocket-Accept`` value for a client key (RFC 6455).
563 
564     ``base64(sha1(client_key + WS_GUID))``. Pure + deterministic so it is
565     unit-tested against the spec example
566     (``dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==`` -> ``s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=``).
567     """
568     digest = _hashlib.sha1(
569         (client_key.strip() + WS_GUID).encode("ascii")).digest()
570     return _b64.b64encode(digest).decode("ascii")
571 
572 
573 def encode_text_frame(text) -> bytes:
574     """Encode a server->client TEXT frame (FIN=1, unmasked — server frames are
575     never masked per RFC 6455)."""
576     if isinstance(text, str):
577         payload = text.encode("utf-8")
578     else:
579         payload = bytes(text)
580     return _encode_frame(WS_OP_TEXT, payload)
581 
582 
583 def encode_close_frame(code=1000, reason=b"") -> bytes:
584     """Encode a server->client CLOSE frame with an optional status code."""
585     if isinstance(reason, str):
586         reason = reason.encode("utf-8")
587     payload = _struct.pack(">H", code) + reason if code is not None else b""
588     return _encode_frame(WS_OP_CLOSE, payload)
589 
590 
591 #: telemetry-resume W6 — the WS ATTACH-ACK control-frame protocol prefix. The
592 #: term_ws stream is otherwise opaque PTY bytes written straight into xterm; a
593 #: structured control message (attach_ack / replay_complete / error) rides the
594 #: SAME token-authed socket as a TEXT frame whose payload begins with this
595 #: prefix. Real PTY output effectively never starts with a NUL byte, so the
596 #: client disambiguates a control frame from terminal bytes by this prefix and
597 #: only swaps in the live pane after ``attach_ack ok:true`` + ``replay_complete``
598 #: — a blank pane becomes a protocol impossibility (NORTH-STAR-AMENDMENT Layer 2).
599 WS_CTL_PREFIX = "\x00ANCHOR-CTL:"
600 
601 
602 def ws_ctl_frame(obj) -> bytes:
603     """Encode a W6 attach-ack control message as a prefixed server TEXT frame."""
604     return encode_text_frame(WS_CTL_PREFIX + json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":")))
605 
606 
607 def encode_pong_frame(payload=b"") -> bytes:
608     """Encode a server->client PONG frame echoing the ping payload."""
609     if isinstance(payload, str):
610         payload = payload.encode("utf-8")
611     return _encode_frame(WS_OP_PONG, payload)
612 
613 
614 def _encode_frame(opcode, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
615     """Build a single unmasked WebSocket frame (FIN=1) for ``opcode``+payload."""
616     b0 = 0x80 | (opcode & 0x0F)            # FIN=1, opcode
617     n = len(payload)
618     if n < 126:
619         header = _struct.pack(">BB", b0, n)
620     elif n < (1 << 16):
621         header = _struct.pack(">BBH", b0, 126, n)
622     else:
623         header = _struct.pack(">BBQ", b0, 127, n)
624     return header + payload
625 
626 
627 #: Max bytes a single client frame's declared payload may be before the codec
628 #: signals a clean close instead of accumulating an unbounded inbuf. Also caps
629 #: the fragmentation-reassembly buffer (FIN=0 TEXT + CONTINUATION run).
630 MAX_WS_FRAME = 1 << 20  # 1 MiB
631 
632 #: A pseudo-opcode the codec emits to tell the pump to close the connection on a
633 #: protocol error (oversized frame, unmasked client data frame, bad fragment).
634 #: It is NOT a real RFC 6455 opcode (0x10 is out of the 4-bit opcode range), so
635 #: it can never collide with a genuine decoded frame.
636 WS_SIGNAL_CLOSE = 0x10
637 
638 
639 def decode_frames(buf: bytes, state=None, require_mask=False):
640     """Decode as many complete WebSocket frames as ``buf`` holds.
641 
642     Returns ``(messages, rest)`` where ``messages`` is a list of
643     ``(opcode, payload_bytes)`` and ``rest`` is the trailing bytes of an
644     incomplete frame to carry forward.
645 
646     ``decode_frames`` is dual-use: the pump decodes CLIENT frames (always masked)
647     and tests decode SERVER frames (never masked). Pass ``require_mask=True``
648     (the pump does) to enforce RFC 6455 §5.1 — an unmasked CLIENT frame is then a
649     protocol error and yields a single ``(WS_SIGNAL_CLOSE, ...)`` message so the
650     pump closes the connection. With ``require_mask=False`` (default) an unmasked
651     frame's payload is taken verbatim (so server→client frames decode cleanly).
652 
653     Bounded (FIX 3): a frame whose DECLARED payload length exceeds
654     :data:`MAX_WS_FRAME` yields ``(WS_SIGNAL_CLOSE, ...)`` instead of buffering
655     toward an allocation — even before the payload bytes arrive.
656 
657     Fragmentation reassembly (FIX 6, RFC 6455 §5.4): a TEXT/BINARY frame with
658     FIN=0 starts a message that is continued by CONTINUATION (opcode 0x0) frames
659     and delivered as ONE message when a CONTINUATION arrives with FIN=1. Control
660     frames (close/ping/pong) are delivered immediately and may interleave a
661     fragmented data message. Reassembly state is carried in the optional
662     ``state`` dict (the pump passes a persistent one); when ``state`` is None a
663     transient one is used (single-buffer/backward-compatible call form). The
664     reassembly buffer is itself bounded by :data:`MAX_WS_FRAME`.
665     """
666     if state is None:
667         state = {}
668     messages = []
669     i = 0
670     n = len(buf)
671     while True:
672         if n - i < 2:
673             break
674         b0 = buf[i]
675         b1 = buf[i + 1]
676         fin = bool(b0 & 0x80)
677         opcode = b0 & 0x0F
678         masked = bool(b1 & 0x80)
679         length = b1 & 0x7F
680         j = i + 2
681         if length == 126:
682             if n - j < 2:
683                 break
684             length = _struct.unpack(">H", buf[j:j + 2])[0]
685             j += 2
686         elif length == 127:
687             if n - j < 8:
688                 break
689             length = _struct.unpack(">Q", buf[j:j + 8])[0]
690             j += 8
691         # Reject an oversized DECLARED payload BEFORE waiting for/allocating it.
692         if length > MAX_WS_FRAME:
693             messages.append((WS_SIGNAL_CLOSE, b"frame too large"))
694             return messages, b""
695         is_control = bool(opcode & 0x8)
696         # RFC 6455 §5.1: a client frame MUST be masked. When decoding client
697         # frames (require_mask), an unmasked frame is a protocol error.
698         if require_mask and not masked:
699             messages.append((WS_SIGNAL_CLOSE, b"unmasked client frame"))
700             return messages, b""
701         mask = b""
702         if masked:
703             if n - j < 4:
704                 break
705             mask = buf[j:j + 4]
706             j += 4
707         if n - j < length:
708             break  # incomplete payload — wait for more bytes
709         payload = bytearray(buf[j:j + length])
710         if masked and mask:
711             for k in range(length):
712                 payload[k] ^= mask[k & 3]
713         payload = bytes(payload)
714         i = j + length
715 
716         if is_control:
717             # Control frames are never fragmented; deliver immediately, even mid
718             # data-message reassembly.
719             messages.append((opcode, payload))
720             continue
721 
722         if opcode == WS_OP_CONT:
723             if "frag_op" not in state:
724                 # CONTINUATION with no message in progress — protocol error.
725                 messages.append((WS_SIGNAL_CLOSE, b"unexpected continuation"))
726                 return messages, b""
727             state["frag_buf"] = state.get("frag_buf", b"") + payload
728             if len(state["frag_buf"]) > MAX_WS_FRAME:
729                 messages.append((WS_SIGNAL_CLOSE, b"fragmented message too large"))
730                 return messages, b""
731             if fin:
732                 messages.append((state.pop("frag_op"), state.pop("frag_buf")))
733             continue
734 
735         # A new TEXT/BINARY data frame.
736         if not fin:
737             # Start of a fragmented message.
738             state["frag_op"] = opcode
739             state["frag_buf"] = payload
740             if len(state["frag_buf"]) > MAX_WS_FRAME:
741                 messages.append((WS_SIGNAL_CLOSE, b"fragmented message too large"))
742                 return messages, b""
743             continue
744         messages.append((opcode, payload))
745     return messages, buf[i:]
746 
747 
748 def _unsafe_path_seg(seg: str) -> bool:
749     """True if a URL segment is unsafe to use as a filesystem path component.
750 
751     Rejects path separators (``/`` ``\\``) and parent-dir traversal (``..``)
752     before the value is used to build a filesystem path. Mirrors the
753     path-traversal hardening on the vendored-KaTeX static route.
754     """
755     if seg is None:
756         return False
757     return "/" in seg or "\\" in seg or ".." in seg

764 ANCHOR_TERM_DIR = ANCHOR_DIR / "vendor" / "anchor-term"
765 ANCHOR_TERM_URL_PREFIX = "/vendor/anchor-term"
766 _ANCHOR_TERM_CONTENT_TYPES = {
767     ".js": "text/javascript; charset=utf-8",

774 def anchor_term_asset(rel_path: str):
775     """Resolve a ``/vendor/anchor-term/<rel>`` request to (bytes, content_type).
776 
777     Path-traversal safe (mirrors ``report_viewer.katex_asset``): the resolved
778     file MUST stay within :data:`ANCHOR_TERM_DIR`. Returns ``None`` for a missing
779     file or an escape attempt.
780     """
781     rel = rel_path.lstrip("/")
782     target = (ANCHOR_TERM_DIR / rel).resolve()
783     try:
784         target.relative_to(ANCHOR_TERM_DIR.resolve())
785     except ValueError:
786         return None
787     if not target.is_file():
788         return None
789     ctype = _ANCHOR_TERM_CONTENT_TYPES.get(target.suffix.lower(),
790                                            "application/octet-stream")
791     return target.read_bytes(), ctype
792

869 # by the ``frontend`` pillar off-switch flag (``pillar_flags``:
870 # ANCHOR_FRONTEND = embedded | static; default embedded = the pre-wave
871 # behavior, byte-identical), so this pillar reverts by FLAG ONLY — flipping

874 # vendored assets above (zero new security surface), with content-hash
875 # cache-busting: ?v=<hash8> is minted per process from the file bytes, so a
876 # new deploy changes the asset URL and a long-lived tab can never pin a stale
877 # copy (the W6 stale-browser criterion).

896 #: home f-string's markup-emitting interpolations stay SERVER-RENDERED as slot
897 #: values — they cannot ride the ANCHOR_BOOT JSON). The raw slot markers live in

903 #: The ANCHOR:SLOT HTML-comment include-slot marker (the W6a substrate
904 #: delimiter, mirrored inline here so product code stays stdlib-only and
905 #: self-contained — ``tools/slot_renderer.py`` is the gate/test twin). This
906 #: comment form (and the W5 project-window ``@@`` form) never appear in real
907 #: frontend content, so neither can collide with page bytes.
908 _HOME_SLOT_RE = re.compile(r"<!--ANCHOR:SLOT:([A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+)-->")
909 
910 
911 def _render_home_slots(shell: str, helpers: dict) -> str:
912     """Substitute every ANCHOR:SLOT include marker in ``shell`` with
913     ``helpers[name]`` (byte-compatible twin of
914     ``tools.slot_renderer.render_slots``).
915 
916     A slot with no helper output, a helper output with no slot, or a non-string
917     output each raises ``ValueError`` LOUDLY — the completeness invariant that
918     makes the extraction provably faithful (never a silent drop / silent extra).
919     """
920     shell_slots = {m.group(1) for m in _HOME_SLOT_RE.finditer(shell)}
921     provided = set(helpers)
922     missing = shell_slots - provided
923     if missing:
924         raise ValueError("home shell slot(s) with no helper output: "
925                          + ", ".join(sorted(missing)))
926     extra = provided - shell_slots
927     if extra:
928         raise ValueError("home helper output(s) with no matching slot: "
929                          + ", ".join(sorted(extra)))
930     for name in shell_slots:
931         if not isinstance(helpers[name], str):
932             raise ValueError(f"home slot {name!r} output must be str, got "
933                              f"{type(helpers[name]).__name__}")
934     return _HOME_SLOT_RE.sub(lambda m: helpers[m.group(1)], shell)
935

987 #: Cache of minted content-hash versions {rel_path: (mtime, size, hash8)}.
988 #: Keyed on the file's (mtime, size) so an EDIT re-mints WITHOUT a restart —
989 #: the once-per-process mint (2026-08-06) served John three rounds of stale UI:
990 #: the page kept referencing the old ?v= while the bytes on disk were new.
991 _static_asset_versions = {}
992 
993 
994 def static_asset_version(rel_path: str) -> str:
995     """The content-hash cache-buster for a static asset (the ``?v=<hash8>``).
996 
997     sha256 of the CURRENT file bytes, first 8 hex chars, re-minted whenever
998     the file's (mtime, size) changes — so a changed file changes every page's
999     asset URL on the next render, restart or not. A missing asset honestly
1000     returns ``"missing"`` and is not cached, healing as soon as it exists.
1001     """
1002     try:
1003         st = (STATIC_DIR / rel_path.lstrip("/")).stat()
1004         key = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
1005     except OSError:
1006         return "missing"
1007     cached = _static_asset_versions.get(rel_path)
1008     if cached is not None and cached[0] == key:
1009         return cached[1]
1010     asset = static_asset(rel_path)
1011     if asset is None:
1012         return "missing"
1013     ver = _hashlib.sha256(asset[0]).hexdigest()[:8]
1014     _static_asset_versions[rel_path] = (key, ver)
1015     return ver
1016 
1017 
1018 def _static_frontend_enabled() -> bool:
1019     """True iff the ``frontend`` pillar flag resolves to ``static`` (W4).
1020 
1021     Resolved FRESH per call through :func:`pillar_flags.current_flags` so a
1022     restartless env flip (tests, ops) is honored. An INVALID flag value falls
1023     back to the embedded (pre-wave) path here — conservative render behavior,
1024     never a 500 dashboard — while the healthcheck's ``check_pillar_state``
1025     assertion fails loudly on the same invalid value, so a misconfiguration
1026     is surfaced, never silently served.
1027     """
1028     try:
1029         return _pillar.current_flags()[_pillar.FLAG_FRONTEND] == "static"
1030     except Exception:
1031         return False

1034 #: Static-frontend bootstrap tail: the legacy page globals the app JS reads
1035 #: (PROJECT_ID · GRASS_DEV_LABEL_PREFIX · ANCHOR_AUTH_REQUIRED) DERIVED from
1036 #: ``window.ANCHOR_BOOT`` client-side — on the static path the bootstrap JSON
1037 #: is the ONLY server→client state channel; no per-page ``var X = <server
1038 #: value>`` injection remains. Plain constant string (zero interpolations).
1039 _PW_BOOT_GLOBALS_JS = (

1080 # ── Project-window SHELL include layer (re-architecture 2026-07 · W5) ────────
1081 # C1 Extraction Increment 2: the project-window HTML/CSS shell lives in two
1082 # module-level plain strings — ``_PW_SHELL_CSS`` (the whole <style> body,
1083 # zero interpolations) and ``_PW_SHELL_TMPL`` (the document shell whose ONLY
1084 # dynamic points are named ``@@slot@@`` placeholders — the include-layer
1085 # design the W1 census's C1 amendment mandated: markup-emitting values are
1086 # computed server-side and injected whole; they cannot ride the ANCHOR_BOOT
1087 # JSON). Both are minted VERBATIM to static files (``static/
1088 # project-window.css`` / ``static/project-window.html``) by
1089 # ``tools/extract_project_window_shell.py`` behind the W5 byte-parity gate;
1090 # until W6 removes the embedded copies the in-source strings stay the single
1091 # source of truth and the files are their derived byte-identical mirrors.
1092 # EMBEDDED (the default) inlines the CSS and fills the in-source template —
1093 # the pre-wave emission, byte-identical. STATIC swaps the inline <style> for
1094 # the hashed static stylesheet link and fills the template read from the
1095 # static FILE (falling back to the in-source twin on a missing/undecodable/
1096 # drifted file so the window still renders correctly, never a 500 — drift is
1097 # the byte-parity GATE's job to catch, not the render path's).
1098 
1099 #: ``@@slot@@`` placeholder syntax for the shell template. ``@@`` appears
1100 #: nowhere in the shell/CSS/JS bodies (gate-checked), so the delimiter can
1101 #: never collide with real frontend content.
1102 _PW_SLOT_RE = re.compile(r"@@([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)@@")
1103 
1104 
1105 def _pw_fill(template: str, slots: dict) -> str:
1106     """Fill ``@@slot@@`` placeholders in ONE regex pass.
1107 
1108     Slot values are inserted verbatim and NEVER re-scanned — user content
1109     containing ``@@…@@`` text can never pull in a second substitution (no
1110     injection through notes/names). An unknown placeholder raises
1111     ``KeyError`` (a drifted template must fail loudly, not render holes).
1112     """
1113     return _PW_SLOT_RE.sub(lambda m: slots[m.group(1)], template)
1114 
1115 
1116 def _pw_shell_template() -> str:
1117     """The shell template the project-window render fills.
1118 
1119     The static path reads it from the static FILE (the W5 "static shell
1120     serving"); embedded — and any static-path miss — uses the in-source
1121     twin, which the gate keeps byte-identical to the file.
1122     """
1123     if _static_frontend_enabled():
1124         asset = static_asset(PROJECT_WINDOW_SHELL_ASSET)
1125         if asset is not None:
1126             try:
1127                 return asset[0].decode("utf-8")
1128             except UnicodeDecodeError:
1129                 pass
1130     return _PW_SHELL_TMPL

1133 # Single-instance project windows (Master Plan C2): opening a project that is
1134 # already open returns the EXISTING instance id rather than spawning a duplicate.
1135 # Server-side, process-local map {project_id: instance_id}. Guarded by the same
1136 # process-wide write lock so concurrent opens resolve to one instance.
1137 _project_instances = {}

1140 def open_project_instance(project_id: str) -> dict:
1141     """Return the (single) window instance for a project, creating if needed.
1142 
1143     Re-opening an already-open project returns the same ``instance_id`` — no
1144     duplicate window (C2). Returns ``{project_id, instance_id, reused}``.
1145     """
1146     with WRITE_LOCK:
1147         existing = _project_instances.get(project_id)
1148         if existing is not None:
1149             return {"project_id": project_id, "instance_id": existing,
1150                     "reused": True}
1151         import uuid as _uuid
1152         inst = _uuid.uuid4().hex
1153         _project_instances[project_id] = inst
1154         return {"project_id": project_id, "instance_id": inst, "reused": False}
1155

1157 def close_project_instance(project_id: str) -> bool:
1158     """Forget a project's open instance (so a later open is fresh)."""

1160         return _project_instances.pop(project_id, None) is not None

1163 def _maybe_git_init(folder: Path) -> bool:
1164     """Optionally run ``git init`` in ``folder``. Best-effort, never raises.
1165 
1166     Returns True if git init was attempted and succeeded. Skipped silently if
1167     git is unavailable or the folder is already a repo.
1168     """
1169     try:
1170         import subprocess
1171         if (folder / ".git").exists():
1172             return False
1173         subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=str(folder), check=True,
1174                        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
1175                        timeout=30, creationflags=_paths.NO_WINDOW)
1176         return True
1177     except Exception:
1178         return False
1179

1181 def _bootstrap_project_best_effort(folder, project_name) -> None:
1182     """Best-effort v8 bootstrap: starter CLAUDE.md + git-init the folder.
1183 
1184     Wired into the register / open / rescan paths so a non-git project doesn't
1185     dead-end a session start with ``not-a-git-repo`` and the keystone (Wave 2
1186     doc persistence) has a repo to commit to. NEVER breaks registration/rescan
1187     if bootstrap fails (try/except → log + skip). Idempotent (an existing repo /
1188     CLAUDE.md is a no-op).
1189     """
1190     try:
1191         if not folder:
1192             return
1193         f = Path(folder)
1194         if not f.is_dir():
1195             return
1196         res = _bootstrap.bootstrap_project(folder, project_name)
1197         git = res.get("git", {})
1198         cm = res.get("claude_md", {})
1199         if git.get("initialized"):
1200             log_change(f"R&D: bootstrap git-init {folder}")
1201         elif not git.get("ok") and git.get("reason") == "git-unavailable":
1202             log_change(f"R&D: bootstrap skipped git-init (git unavailable) {folder}")
1203         if cm.get("created"):
1204             log_change(f"R&D: bootstrap wrote starter CLAUDE.md {folder}")
1205     except Exception:
1206         pass  # bootstrap is best-effort; never block registration/open/rescan
1207 
1208 
1209 def resolve_project_dir(parent_path, name: str) -> Path:
1210     """Computes the on-disk project directory and prevents double-nesting.
1211 
1212     If parent_path already ends with name (case/sep-insensitive),
1213     do NOT append name again.
1214     """
1215     p_str = str(parent_path).replace('\\', '/').rstrip('/')
1216     n_str = str(name).replace('\\', '/').strip('/')
1217     parent = Path(p_str).expanduser()
1218     if parent.name.lower() == n_str.lower():
1219         return parent
1220     return parent / n_str
1221 
1222 
1223 def create_new_folder_project(name: str, parent_path, priority: int = 2,
1224                               git_init: bool = False) -> dict:
1225     """+ New Project / create-new-folder mode.
1226 
1227     Creates ``<parent>/<name>`` (optional ``git init``), registers a project
1228     with a FRESH id, and scaffolds ``.anchor/projects/<id>/{lanes}/``. Returns
1229     the registry entry plus ``folder_created`` / ``git_initialized`` flags.
1230     """
1231     with WRITE_LOCK:
1232         parent = Path(parent_path).expanduser()
1233         folder = resolve_project_dir(parent, name)
1234         folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1235         git_done = _maybe_git_init(folder) if git_init else False
1236         # v8 Wave 1: always bootstrap (starter CLAUDE.md + git-init if absent) so
1237         # a session start never dead-ends on not-a-git-repo. Idempotent + best-
1238         # effort; honors the explicit git_init above (a no-op if already a repo).
1239         _bootstrap_project_best_effort(folder, name)
1240         entry = _rnd.add_project(name, str(folder), priority=priority,
1241                                  scaffold=True)
1242         log_change(f"R&D: created project '{name}' at {folder} (id {entry['id']})")
1243         set_project_setup_status(entry["id"], "Setting up the project…")
1244         try:
1245             discover_and_adopt(entry["id"], auto_read=True)
1246         except Exception:
1247             pass
1248         finally:
1249             if str(project_setup_statuses().get(entry["id"], "")).startswith(
1250                     "Setting up"):
1251                 set_project_setup_status(entry["id"], None)
1252         return {"entry": entry, "folder_created": True,
1253                 "git_initialized": git_done}
1254 
1255 
1256 def select_existing_project(name: str, folder_path, priority: int = 2) -> dict:
1257     """+ New Project / select-existing mode.
1258 
1259     Registers the chosen folder as a project (fresh id, isolated store). Adding
1260     another project for a folder that already hosts projects is allowed
1261     (1 folder : N projects). A missing path still registers but surfaces a
1262     ``path-missing`` state on read (no crash).
1263     """
1264     with WRITE_LOCK:
1265         folder = Path(folder_path).expanduser()
1266         exists = folder.exists()
1267         # v8 Wave 1: bootstrap an existing folder on register — starter CLAUDE.md
1268         # + git-init if it isn't a repo — so a research/build session start on it
1269         # no longer returns not-a-git-repo. Best-effort + idempotent; skipped for
1270         # a missing path (nothing to bootstrap).
1271         if exists:
1272             _bootstrap_project_best_effort(folder, name)
1273         entry = _rnd.add_project(name, str(folder), priority=priority,
1274                                  scaffold=exists)
1275         if not exists:
1276             # Don't fabricate a store under a missing path; mark it so the view
1277             # shows path-missing rather than crashing.
1278             entry = dict(entry)
1279             entry["state"] = _rnd.STATE_PATH_MISSING
1280         existing = _rnd.group_by_folder().get(str(folder), [])
1281         log_change(f"R&D: registered project '{name}' at {folder} (id {entry['id']})")
1282         # Brownfield discover/adopt runs in the BACKGROUND (2026-08-26). It used
1283         # to run inline, inside WRITE_LOCK, and it fires the first-scan Gandalf
1284         # read — on a large folder (the reported case: 270GB / 25k files) the
1285         # POST never got a response, so the dashboard never reloaded, so John
1286         # clicked "Create" again and registered a DUPLICATE. Registration is the
1287         # only thing the click is waiting for; everything after it is discovery.
1288         if exists:
1289             # Announce BEFORE the thread starts, so the card carries the
1290             # message from the first render after the page reloads.
1291             set_project_setup_status(
1292                 entry["id"], "Setting up the project — reading what is here…")
1293 
1294             def _adopt_bg(pid=entry["id"]):
1295                 try:
1296                     # auto_read is back ON for registration (John, 2026-08-27:
1297                     # he wants the read, he wanted to be TOLD about it). What
1298                     # made this dangerous was never the read itself — it was
1299                     # three unannounced swarms at once; the machine-wide
1300                     # one-at-a-time cap is what fixed that.
1301                     discover_and_adopt(pid, auto_read=True)
1302                 except Exception:
1303                     pass
1304                 finally:
1305                     # clear only OUR "setting up" message: a deferral notice
1306                     # written during the read scheduling must survive
1307                     if str(project_setup_statuses().get(pid, "")).startswith(
1308                             "Setting up"):
1309                         set_project_setup_status(pid, None)
1310             # Backgrounded in the SERVER; inline under the same flag the rest
1311             # of the proactive machinery uses, so the test suite stays
1312             # deterministic (a daemon thread writing project state mid-suite
1313             # made a neighbouring summary-cache assertion flap).
1314             if _PROACTIVE_SUMMARY_ENABLED:
1315                 try:
1316                     threading.Thread(target=_adopt_bg, daemon=True).start()
1317                 except Exception:
1318                     _adopt_bg()
1319             else:
1320                 _adopt_bg()
1321         return {"entry": entry, "path_exists": exists,
1322                 "siblings_in_folder": [e for e in existing
1323                                        if e["id"] != entry["id"]]}
1324 
1325 
1326 def discover_and_adopt(project_id: str, auto_read: bool = True) -> dict:
1327     """One brownfield pipeline: scan -> adopt -> reconcile -> write marker.
1328 
1329     Called from register (``add_project`` wiring), open (``GET /project/<id>``),
1330     and the manual Rescan (``POST /api/rnd/rescan``). Idempotent, bounded, and
1331     robust to a missing/huge/UNC/mistyped folder (returns a no-op report, never
1332     hangs/raises). Discovered records are reconciled (pruned when their artifact
1333     is gone); real efforts are never touched. The marker (``Anchor.md`` +
1334     sidecar) is rewritten ONLY when its structure changed (no-churn).
1335 
1336     Returns ``{"ok": bool, "scanned": <counts>, "adopt": <report>,
1337     "marker": <report>}``.
1338     """
1339     proj = _rnd.get_project(project_id)
1340     if proj is None:
1341         return {"ok": False, "reason": "unknown-project"}
1342     folder = (proj or {}).get("folder_path", "")
1343     try:
1344         if not folder or not Path(folder).is_dir():
1345             return {"ok": False, "reason": "path-missing"}
1346     except OSError:
1347         return {"ok": False, "reason": "path-missing"}
1348 
1349     # v8 Wave 1: bootstrap on open/rescan (this is the rescan path AND the open
1350     # path via GET /project/<id>) — starter CLAUDE.md + git-init if the folder
1351     # isn't a repo. Best-effort + idempotent; heals a non-git project so a later
1352     # session start succeeds.
1353     _bootstrap_project_best_effort(folder, (proj or {}).get("name", ""))
1354 
1355     scan = _bscan.scan(folder)
1356     adopt = _eh.adopt_discovered(folder, project_id, scan)
1357     # Reconcile is implicit in adopt (prunes stale discovered), but run an
1358     # explicit pass too so a deleted artifact whose lane vanished is pruned.
1359     _eh.reconcile_discovered(folder, project_id)
1360     # Folder-history unification (Wave 2, scope #1): also adopt trio sessions
1361     # found in OTHER project-ids' stores for the SAME folder, so a run recorded
1362     # under a sibling id is not invisible to this project. Non-destructive — the
1363     # sibling stores/ids are left intact (the explicit, reviewable
1364     # ``reconcile_folder`` is what folds + hard-deletes them).
1365     sibling = _eh.adopt_sibling_sessions(folder, project_id)
1366     marker = _marker.write_anchor_md(folder)
1367     # Wave 5 (v3): proactively (re)generate the accurate cached PROJECT summary
1368     # off the render path. We force a regenerate here so a rescan picks up new
1369     # plan docs / deliverables; the dashboard render only READS the cache.
1370     _trigger_project_summary(folder, project_id, force=True)
1371     # Wave 6 (v3): proactively generate per-session summaries that lack a cache,
1372     # so an expanded session accordion serves a ready cache rather than a
1373     # "generating…" fallback. Background + gated like the project summary.
1374     _trigger_project_session_summaries(folder, project_id)
1375     # Gandalf v1 (decision #4): on first scan ONLY, kick off the honest project
1376     # read. first-run-ONLY (check-and-set BEFORE scheduling — no TOCTOU) + gated
1377     # by _PROACTIVE_SUMMARY_ENABLED (off in tests) + background daemon. Never
1378     # blocks the rescan/render path.
1379     # auto_read is a seam, not a policy: registration passes True again as of
1380     # 2026-08-27 (John wants the read — it produced a real verdict), and what
1381     # keeps it safe is the machine-wide one-at-a-time cap inside the trigger,
1382     # not skipping the read. Kept as a parameter so a caller that genuinely
1383     # must not spend a read can still say so.
1384     if auto_read:
1385         _trigger_gandalf_first_scan(folder, project_id)
1386     return {"ok": True, "scanned": dict(scan.counts), "adopt": adopt,
1387             "sibling_adopt": sibling, "marker": marker}
1388 
1389 
1390 _PROJECT_OPEN_DISCOVERY_LOCK = threading.Lock()
1391 _PROJECT_OPEN_DISCOVERY_INFLIGHT = set()
1392 
1393 
1394 def _start_project_open_discovery(project_id: str, *, authorized: bool) -> bool:
1395     """Start at most one authenticated open-scan for ``project_id``.
1396 
1397     A document GET used to mint an unbounded daemon thread before its token
1398     check. Besides allowing unauthenticated writes/bootstrap, repeated opens
1399     could fan out the same expensive scan. Returns ``True`` only when this call
1400     actually starts a worker; failures and duplicates are honest ``False``.
1401     """
1402     pid = str(project_id or "").strip()
1403     if not authorized or not pid or pid == "__dashboard__":
1404         return False
1405     with _PROJECT_OPEN_DISCOVERY_LOCK:
1406         if pid in _PROJECT_OPEN_DISCOVERY_INFLIGHT:
1407             return False
1408         _PROJECT_OPEN_DISCOVERY_INFLIGHT.add(pid)
1409 
1410     def _run():
1411         try:
1412             discover_and_adopt(pid)
1413         except Exception as exc:
1414             _logger.error("project-open discovery failed for %s: %s", pid, exc)
1415         finally:
1416             with _PROJECT_OPEN_DISCOVERY_LOCK:
1417                 _PROJECT_OPEN_DISCOVERY_INFLIGHT.discard(pid)
1418 
1419     try:
1420         threading.Thread(target=_run, daemon=True,
1421                          name="discover-" + pid[:24]).start()
1422         return True
1423     except Exception as exc:
1424         with _PROJECT_OPEN_DISCOVERY_LOCK:
1425             _PROJECT_OPEN_DISCOVERY_INFLIGHT.discard(pid)
1426         _logger.error("project-open discovery could not start for %s: %s",
1427                       pid, exc)
1428         return False
1429

1434 #: ``ANCHOR_PROACTIVE_SUMMARY=1``. When OFF, summaries are still generated
1435 #: lazily/on demand (and the render path always just reads the cache).
1436 _PROACTIVE_SUMMARY_ENABLED = (

1438     in ("1", "true", "yes", "on"))

1441 def _proactive_summary_pref(raw) -> bool:
1442     """v1.1.3: the server main()'s background-summary decision, testable.
1443 
1444     False ONLY for an EXPLICIT off (``0/false/no/off``) — the shared-install
1445     opt-out ``share_onboard.spawn_anchor_server`` sets, so Anchor never spends
1446     a collaborator's subscription without an explicit action. Unset/anything
1447     else keeps the author default: force-on in ``main()``.
1448     """
1449     return (raw or "").strip().lower() not in ("0", "false", "no", "off")

1480 def _zh_node_base():

1484 def _zh_node_is_up(timeout=1.0):
1485     """True when the System-Wide Sentinel on :48484 answers /api/state."""
1486     import urllib.request
1487     try:
1488         with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{_zh_node_base()}/api/state", timeout=timeout) as r:
1489             return 200 <= getattr(r, "status", 200) < 500
1490     except Exception:
1491         return False

1494 def _zh_node_is_stale(timeout=1.0):
1495     """True when the running hunter GUI was started from an OLDER server.js than
1496     the one on disk (2026-09-04): the process outlives service restarts and
1497     keeps the code + environment it was born with, so a picker rule or a prefs
1498     env change never reached it until someone killed it by hand. The hunter
1499     reports ``server_mtime`` in /api/state; a hunter that reports none is an
1500     old build and therefore stale."""
1501     import json as _json
1502     import urllib.request
1503     try:
1504         with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{_zh_node_base()}/api/state", timeout=timeout) as r:
1505             st = _json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8", "replace") or "{}")
1506     except Exception:
1507         return False  # not up / unreadable — the caller's liveness logic decides
1508     try:
1509         reported = float(st.get("server_mtime") or 0)
1510         on_disk = os.path.getmtime(_ZH_NODE_SERVER_PATH) * 1000.0
1511     except Exception:
1512         return False
1513     return reported <= 0 or (on_disk - reported) > 2000.0
