21955 class AnchorHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
21956     #: Query params whose VALUES must never reach a log file.
21957     _LOG_REDACT_PARAMS = ("token", "capability", "nonce", "key", "secret")
21958 
21959     @classmethod
21960     def _redact_request_line(cls, line):
21961         """Strip secret query-param values from an access-log request line.
21962 
21963         2026-07-26 hardening. Every authed GET carried the LIVE capability token
21964         verbatim into ``logs/nssm-stdout.log`` (the GET-transport ``?token=``
21965         design), forever — in the very directory a collaborator is told to
21966         inspect when something breaks. The token is redacted here, at the one
21967         place request lines are written, so no call site can forget.
21968         """
21969         import re as _re  # module-local: anchor_gui imports re per-function
21970         try:
21971             s = str(line)
21972         except Exception:
21973             return line
21974         for p in cls._LOG_REDACT_PARAMS:
21975             s = _re.sub(r"(?i)([?&]" + _re.escape(p) + r"=)[^&\s\"']+",
21976                         r"\1<redacted>", s)
21977         return s
21978 
21979     def log_message(self, format, *args):
21980         first = self._redact_request_line(args[0]) if args else ""
21981         print(f"  [{datetime.now().strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {first}")
21982 
21983     def log_error(self, format, *args):
21984         # Quiet the benign client-disconnect noise the base class would log to
21985         # stderr (it routes BrokenPipe/ConnectionReset/timeout messages here).
21986         # Real protocol errors still surface via the normal response paths.
21987         return
21988 
21989     def _steward_same_origin(self):
21990         """Defense-in-depth CSRF guard on the steward routes (the token is the
21991         PRIMARY control — every /api/steward/* call is token-gated before this
21992         runs; the chamber has no equivalent guard at all).
21993 
21994         SAME-ORIGIN generally, not localhost-only (2026-08-25): John's work
21995         desktop reaches Anchor over Tailscale, where the Host header is the
21996         machine's tailnet name — the old localhost-only gate 403'd every
21997         cockpit data call from there (shell loaded, no tiles, no persona
21998         icon). We now refuse only POSITIVE cross-site evidence:
21999         - fetch-metadata marking the call cross-site, or
22000         - an Origin header naming a different host than the Host header
22001           (allowing the reverse-proxy case — Tailscale Serve 443→8777 —
22002           where the proxy rewrites Host to loopback while the browser's
22003           Origin keeps the public name)."""
22004         sfs = self.headers.get("Sec-Fetch-Site")
22005         if sfs and sfs not in ("same-origin", "same-site", "none"):
22006             return False
22007         host = (self.headers.get("Host") or "").strip().lower()
22008         host_bare = host.split(":")[0]
22009         host_local = (host_bare in ("127.0.0.1", "localhost")
22010                       or host.startswith("[::1]"))
22011         origin = (self.headers.get("Origin") or "").strip().lower()
22012         if (origin and host and not host_local
22013                 and origin.split("://")[-1] != host):
22014             return False
22015         return True
22016 
22017     def _steward_pid_dir(self, pid):
22018         """Resolve a project id to its campaign folder for the cockpit."""
22019         proj = _rnd.get_project(pid) or {}
22020         folder = (proj.get("folder_path") or "").strip()
22021         return folder if folder and os.path.isdir(folder) else None
22022 
22023     def _steward_api(self, method, verb, body=None):
22024         """Dispatch a /api/steward/<verb> call to the cockpit mount, scoped to
22025         the project id carried in ?pid= (GET) or the JSON body (POST)."""
22026         if not self._steward_same_origin():
22027             self._send_json({"error": "cross-origin refused"}, code=403); return
22028         try:
22029             from steward_cockpit import steward_routes as _scr
22030             from steward_cockpit import steward_engine as _se
22031             _scr.CONFIG["steward"] = (_steward_ui().get("label") or "Ecgberht")
22032             # (2026-08-25) the effort-name guard refuses the live token — a
22033             # token paste became an effort's directory name once
22034             _scr.CONFIG["anchor_token"] = _paths.expected_token() or ""
22035             # runtime state lives OUTSIDE the repo (Anchor's W11 invariant) - not
22036             # in steward_cockpit/, where it would be committed/pushed and keep git
22037             # dirty. Point it at the Anchor data dir (idempotent).
22038             try:
22039                 _se.STATE_FILE = _paths.data_dir() / "steward-cockpit-state.json"
22040             except Exception:
22041                 pass
22042             _q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)
22043             _qpid = (_q.get("pid") or [""])[0]
22044             if method == "GET":
22045                 qs = {k: v[0] for k, v in _q.items()}
22046                 proot = self._steward_pid_dir(_qpid)
22047                 if proot is None:
22048                     self._send_json({"error": "unknown project"}, code=404); return
22049                 obj, code = _scr.api_get(proot, verb, qs)
22050             else:
22051                 # the client shim carries pid in the URL query for POST too;
22052                 # accept it from the body OR the query
22053                 pid = (body or {}).get("pid") or _qpid
22054                 proot = self._steward_pid_dir(pid)
22055                 if proot is None:
22056                     self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "unknown project"}, code=404); return
22057                 obj, code = _scr.api_post(proot, verb, body or {})
22058             # Deliverable file streaming (2026-08-25): the routes layer returns a
22059             # {__file__, __ctype__} marker (containment already enforced there);
22060             # everything else stays JSON.
22061             if code == 200 and isinstance(obj, dict) and "__notebook_redirect__" in obj:
22062                 # Authorization already succeeded. Never forward Anchor's
22063                 # token/cookie to Jupyter or leak it in a Referer header.
22064                 self.send_response(302)
22065                 self.send_header("Location", obj["__notebook_redirect__"])
22066                 self.send_header("Referrer-Policy", "no-referrer")
22067                 self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
22068                 self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
22069                 self.end_headers()
22070                 return
22071             if code == 200 and isinstance(obj, dict) and "__html__" in obj:
22072                 # (2026-09-04) a rendered preview page (Office deliverables)
22073                 self._send_html(obj["__html__"])
22074                 return
22075             if code == 200 and isinstance(obj, dict) and "__file__" in obj:
22076                 try:
22077                     with open(obj["__file__"], "rb") as fh:
22078                         raw = fh.read()
22079                     self.send_response(200)
22080                     self.send_header("Content-Type", obj.get("__ctype__", "application/octet-stream"))
22081                     self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
22082                     if obj.get("__csp__"):
22083                         # a project's own HTML/SVG renders in an OPAQUE origin (2026-09-06)
22084                         self.send_header("Content-Security-Policy", obj["__csp__"])
22085                     self.send_header("Content-Disposition",
22086                                      '%s; filename="%s"' % (obj.get("__disposition__") or "inline",
22087                                                             os.path.basename(obj["__file__"]).replace('"', '')))
22088                     self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
22089                     self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(raw)))
22090                     self.end_headers()
22091                     self.wfile.write(raw)
22092                 except Exception as exc:
22093                     if not _is_benign_disconnect(exc):
22094                         self._send_json({"error": "deliverable read failed: " + str(exc)}, code=500)
22095                 return
22096             self._send_json(obj, code=code)
22097         except Exception as exc:
22098             if _is_benign_disconnect(exc):
22099                 return
22100             self._send_json({"error": "steward: " + str(exc)}, code=500)
22101 
22102     def _send_json(self, data, code=200):
22103         body = json.dumps(data).encode()
22104         try:
22105             self.send_response(code)
22106             self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
22107             self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
22108             self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
22109             self.end_headers()
22110             self.wfile.write(body)
22111         except Exception as exc:
22112             # Client closed mid-response (browser tab close / Playwright
22113             # teardown). Nothing left to send — swallow ONLY the benign
22114             # disconnect; re-raise anything else.
22115             if _is_benign_disconnect(exc):
22116                 return
22117             raise
22118 
22119     def _send_html(self, html_text, cookie=None):
22120         try:
22121             from high_seat_page import with_tab_icon as _with_tab_icon
22122             html_text = _with_tab_icon(html_text, BUILD_ID)   # every page wears his anchor in its tab (2026-10-01)
22123         except Exception as _e:                               # the page goes as it was; the log says why (Grok W3d)
22124             print("  [%s] TAB ICON rewrite failed: %r" % (datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S"), _e))
22125         body = html_text.encode("utf-8")
22126         try:
22127             self.send_response(200)
22128             self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
22129             self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
22130             self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate")
22131             self.send_header("Pragma", "no-cache")
22132             self.send_header("Expires", "0")
22133             if cookie:
22134                 self.send_header("Set-Cookie", cookie)      # the local browser's login, set by the page itself (2026-10-01)
22135             self.end_headers()
22136             self.wfile.write(body)
22137         except Exception as exc:
22138             if _is_benign_disconnect(exc):
22139                 return
22140             raise
22141 
22142     def _send_bytes(self, data, content_type, cache="no-cache"):
22143         try:
22144             self.send_response(200)
22145             self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
22146             self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
22147             self.send_header("Cache-Control", cache)
22148             self.end_headers()
22149             self.wfile.write(data)
22150         except Exception as exc:
22151             if _is_benign_disconnect(exc):
22152                 return
22153             raise
22154 
22155     # ── SSE for the interactive terminal (Wave 7) ────────────────────────────
22156     def _sse_event(self, event, data_obj):
22157         """Write ONE well-formed SSE event frame and flush it.
22158 
22159         Frame shape (per the SSE spec): an ``event:`` line, one ``data:`` line
22160         carrying a JSON payload, then a BLANK line terminating the event. Flushed
22161         immediately so a streaming client observes events as they arrive.
22162 
22163         Teardown hardening: writing/flushing onto a ``wfile`` whose underlying
22164         socket was already closed (client gone, or the request thread torn down
22165         out from under a leaked pump) raises ``ValueError("I/O operation on
22166         closed file")`` — which is a benign client-gone condition, not a server
22167         bug, but it is NOT in the OSError family the stream loops guard on. We
22168         normalize it to a ``BrokenPipeError`` so the existing
22169         ``except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError)`` guards end
22170         the stream CLEANLY (the daemon thread never raises a stray ValueError on
22171         teardown). The benign socket-teardown OSErrors propagate unchanged for
22172         those same guards; any non-benign error is re-raised untouched.
22173         """
22174         payload = json.dumps(data_obj, ensure_ascii=False)
22175         frame = f"event: {event}\ndata: {payload}\n\n"
22176         try:
22177             self.wfile.write(frame.encode("utf-8"))
22178             self.wfile.flush()
22179         except ValueError as exc:
22180             # I/O on a closed file (wfile closed under us) == client/connection
22181             # gone. Re-raise as BrokenPipeError so the OSError-family guards
22182             # catch it; never swallow a different ValueError.
22183             if "closed file" in str(exc):
22184                 raise BrokenPipeError(str(exc)) from exc
22185             raise
22186 
22187     def _serve_term_sse(self):
22188         """Stream a terminal session's output as Server-Sent Events.
22189 
22190         Stdlib-only streaming: a chunked ``text/event-stream`` response that
22191         loops, polling :func:`rnd_terminal.read_since` for new output, flushing an
22192         ``output`` event for new lines, a ``status`` event on change, and a
22193         ``gate`` event when an in-session prompt surfaces. It emits a
22194         ``heartbeat`` every few idle ticks and ENDS with a ``done`` event when the
22195         session is terminal OR a bounded tick budget elapses — so a test can read
22196         N events and the stream closes (no indefinite hang). The bound + poll
22197         interval are query-overridable for fast hermetic tests.
22198         """
22199         q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)
22200         session = (q.get("session", [""])[0] or "").strip()
22201         try:
22202             since = int(q.get("since", ["0"])[0] or 0)
22203         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22204             since = 0
22205         if not session:
22206             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "missing session"}, 400)
22207             return
22208         # Bounded loop knobs (defaults are production-sane; tests shrink them so
22209         # the stream ends quickly). poll_interval in seconds; max_ticks bounds the
22210         # total loop iterations; heartbeat_every emits a keep-alive on idle ticks.
22211         try:
22212             poll_interval = float(q.get("poll", ["0.25"])[0] or 0.25)
22213         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22214             poll_interval = 0.25
22215         try:
22216             max_ticks = int(q.get("max_ticks", ["240"])[0] or 240)
22217         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22218             max_ticks = 240
22219         try:
22220             heartbeat_every = int(q.get("hb", ["8"])[0] or 8)
22221         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22222             heartbeat_every = 8
22223 
22224         self.send_response(200)
22225         self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream; charset=utf-8")
22226         self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache, no-store")
22227         self.send_header("Connection", "close")
22228         # No Content-Length → chunked/streamed body via the connection close.
22229         self.end_headers()
22230 
22231         cursor = since
22232         last_status = None
22233         idle = 0
22234         try:
22235             for _tick in range(max(1, max_ticks)):
22236                 # Guard the per-tick read + event emission so ANY exception from
22237                 # read_since (not just pipe/OS errors) ends the stream CLEANLY
22238                 # with a terminal done/error event instead of letting the handler
22239                 # thread crash mid-stream and leaving the client hung (never
22240                 # getting a 'done'). Pipe/connection errors mean the client is
22241                 # already gone, so for those we just stop without trying to write.
22242                 try:
22243                     out = _term.read_since(session, cursor)
22244                     lines = out.get("lines") or []
22245                     if lines:
22246                         self._sse_event("output", {"lines": lines,
22247                                                    "next": out.get("next", cursor)})
22248                         cursor = out.get("next", cursor)
22249                         idle = 0
22250                     else:
22251                         idle += 1
22252                     status = out.get("status")
22253                     if status and status != last_status:
22254                         self._sse_event("status", {"status": status})
22255                         last_status = status
22256                     pending = out.get("pending_prompt")
22257                     if pending:
22258                         self._sse_event("gate", {"prompt": pending})
22259                     if status in _term.TERMINAL_STATUSES:
22260                         # Drain any final lines, then end the stream cleanly.
22261                         final = _term.read_since(session, cursor)
22262                         fl = final.get("lines") or []
22263                         if fl:
22264                             self._sse_event("output", {"lines": fl,
22265                                                        "next": final.get("next", cursor)})
22266                             cursor = final.get("next", cursor)
22267                         self._sse_event("done", {"status": status, "next": cursor})
22268                         return
22269                     if heartbeat_every and idle and idle % heartbeat_every == 0:
22270                         self._sse_event("heartbeat", {"next": cursor})
22271                 except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):
22272                     # Client closed the connection — stop cleanly (re-raise to the
22273                     # outer guard, which simply returns).
22274                     raise
22275                 except Exception:
22276                     # ANY other failure (a generic read_since error, a bad record,
22277                     # etc.): emit a final error-flavored done so the client always
22278                     # gets a terminal frame, then end the stream. Best-effort — if
22279                     # even this write fails the outer guard swallows it.
22280                     try:
22281                         self._sse_event("done", {"status": "error",
22282                                                  "next": cursor, "error": True})
22283                     except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):
22284                         pass
22285                     return
22286                 time.sleep(max(0.0, poll_interval))
22287             # Tick budget exhausted while still live — end with a heartbeat-flavored
22288             # done so the client can re-open (bounded, never an infinite hold).
22289             self._sse_event("done", {"status": last_status or "running",
22290                                      "next": cursor, "bounded": True})
22291         except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):
22292             # Client closed the connection — stop cleanly.
22293             return
22294 
22295     # ── ConPTY terminal transport (Wave 3) ──────────────────────────────────
22296     def _term_token_ok(self):
22297         """Auth a token-gated GET endpoint (``?token=`` / Authorization header).
22298 
22299         Browsers can't set request headers on an EventSource / WebSocket
22300         handshake, so the terminal GET surface (an RCE surface) authenticates via
22301         a query-param token with the SAME semantics as ``paths.auth_ok``: if no
22302         token is configured (``ANCHOR_TOKEN`` unset) it is allowed (local
22303         back-compat); otherwise the provided token must match.
22304 
22305         rearch-2026-07 W2: the standard ``Authorization`` header (Bearer or a
22306         bare token) is accepted EVERYWHERE this gate applies, so every
22307         non-browser consumer (healthcheck endpoint walk, scripts) has a header
22308         token path — ``?token=`` remains only because the WS/SSE transports
22309         demand it. Also accepts a token carried in the
22310         ``Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`` header (for WS clients).
22311         """
22312         # 2026-10-01: ANY valid credential this request carries is enough - the query token, the Authorization
22313         # header, the WS subprotocol, or the HttpOnly auth cookie (rearch W9). Before, the first one seen was the
22314         # only one judged, so a stale saved token in a header refused a browser whose cookie was good.
22315         q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)
22316         presented = [q.get("token", [None])[0],
22317                      _paths.token_from_authorization(self.headers.get("Authorization")),
22318                      self.headers.get("Sec-WebSocket-Protocol"),
22319                      _paths.token_from_cookie(self.headers.get("Cookie"))]
22320         presented = [t for t in presented if t]
22321         if not presented:
22322             return _paths.auth_ok(None)      # nothing carried: the configured policy answers (allowed only when no token is set)
22323         return any(_paths.auth_ok(t) for t in presented)
22324 
22325     def _auth_shape(self):
22326         """One line saying what this request carried for the gate - never a value (2026-10-01, the box that stayed on
22327         his screen while every probe passed): peer, Host, cookie none/valid/stale, Authorization none/valid/stale, query
22328         token none/valid/stale, fetch-metadata mode, the user agent's head, and whether the local-browser rule held."""
22329         try:
22330             def judge(t):
22331                 return "none" if not t else ("valid" if _paths.auth_ok(t) else "stale")
22332             q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)
22333             addr = getattr(self, "client_address", None)
22334             ua = str(self.headers.get("User-Agent") or "")[:60].replace(" ", "_")
22335             return ("peer=%s host=%s cookie=%s auth=%s qtoken=%s sfm=%s fwd=%s local=%s ua=%s" % (
22336                 (addr or ("?",))[0], str(self.headers.get("Host") or "-"), judge(_paths.token_from_cookie(self.headers.get("Cookie"))),
22337                 judge(_paths.token_from_authorization(self.headers.get("Authorization"))), judge(q.get("token", [None])[0]),
22338                 str(self.headers.get("Sec-Fetch-Mode") or "-"), "yes" if (self.headers.get("X-Forwarded-For") or self.headers.get("X-Forwarded-Proto")) else "no",
22339                 _local_browser(self), ua))
22340         except Exception as e:
22341             return "auth-shape unreadable: %s" % e
22342 
22343     def _locked_page(self):
22344         """His word, 2026-10-03 ("lock the dashboard and Doctor too", after the Cave): a PAGE that shows the record is
22345         answered with the lock page (high_seat_page.render_locked_html: the anchor and a token box) when a token is
22346         required and this request carries no valid credential (cookie, header, query token) and is not this machine's
22347         own browser (which _local_login_cookie logs in). Returns (locked_html_or_None, cookie_to_set)."""
22348         _ck = self._local_login_cookie()
22349         if not _paths.expected_token() or _ck or self._term_token_ok():
22350             return None, _ck
22351         from high_seat_page import render_locked_html
22352         return render_locked_html({"build": BUILD_ID}), None
22353 
22354     def _local_login_cookie(self):
22355         """A Set-Cookie value for a PAGE served to this machine's own browser (see _local_browser) that carries no
22356         valid cookie yet, so its later reads and sends ride the cookie (thirty days) with nothing pasted; None
22357         otherwise. The page is the only place that trusts the local browser; every API gate stays strict."""
22358         try:
22359             want = _paths.expected_token()
22360             if not want or not _local_browser(self):
22361                 return None
22362             have = _paths.token_from_cookie(self.headers.get("Cookie"))
22363             if have and _paths.auth_ok(have):
22364                 return None
22365             return _paths.build_auth_cookie(want, secure=_request_is_secure(self))
22366         except Exception:
22367             return None
22368 
22369     # ── Strangler dispatch (rearch W7 / C2) ─────────────────────────────────
22370     def _route_auth_ok(self, route):
22371         """Apply a route row's declared auth policy. True == permitted.
22372 
22373         ``open`` routes are always permitted. For ``token``/``ws_token`` routes:
22374         a POST is already gated by the do_POST token middleware (which runs
22375         BEFORE the strangler), so re-checking would be redundant AND wrong (that
22376         middleware also accepts the X-Anchor-Token header and a body token, which
22377         :meth:`_term_token_ok` does not) — so a POST returns True here. A GET is
22378         gated via :meth:`_term_token_ok` (query token / Authorization header),
22379         matching the pre-existing token-gated GET surface exactly.
22380         """
22381         if route.auth == _routes.AUTH_OPEN:
22382             return True
22383         if route.method == "POST":
22384             return True
22385         return self._term_token_ok()
22386 
22387     def _strangler_dispatch(self, method, path, body=None):
22388         """Table-first dispatch. Returns True iff this request was HANDLED here.
22389 
22390         Looks the request up in the declarative route table. A matched, MIGRATED
22391         row is handled by its module-level function — but the row's auth check is
22392         invoked FIRST (honestly special-cased for ``kind != standard``: the auth
22393         gate runs before any stream/upgrade handler takes over the socket). A
22394         miss, or a matched-but-not-yet-migrated row, returns False so the caller
22395         FALLS THROUGH to the legacy if/elif chain unchanged (the strangler
22396         pattern). Defensive: a row flagged migrated whose handler name is not
22397         registered also falls through rather than 500-ing.
22398         """
22399         route = _routes.match(method, path)
22400         if route is None or not route.migrated:
22401             return False
22402         fn = _MIGRATED_HANDLERS.get(route.handler)
22403         if fn is None:
22404             return False
22405         if not self._route_auth_ok(route):
22406             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "unauthorized"}, 401)
22407             return True
22408         # Always hand handlers the FULL request URI (query included). Route
22409         # matching uses a path-only string, but handlers that parse ?project_id=
22410         # must see the query. Passing path-only caused tidy_idy_status to return
22411         # "project_id required" on every remote poll (Tailscale freeze at 42%).
22412         full = getattr(self, "path", None) or path
22413         fn(self, full, body)
22414         return True
22415 
22416     # ── Data-plane auth-mode gate (rearch W8 warn / W9 enforce) ──────────────
22417     def _auth_mode(self):
22418         """The current ``auth`` pillar flag: ``open`` | ``warn`` | ``enforce``.
22419 
22420         Resolved from the environment each call (``ANCHOR_AUTH_MODE`` / the
22421         ``ANCHOR_AUTH_WARN`` alias). Defensive: an unreadable/invalid config
22422         falls back to ``open`` (today's live behavior) rather than crashing a
22423         request — the loud invalid-value failure is the healthcheck's job
22424         (``check_pillar_state``), not the hot request path's.
22425         """
22426         try:
22427             return _pillar_flags.current_flags()[_pillar_flags.FLAG_AUTH]
22428         except Exception:
22429             return _pillar_flags.FLAG_DEFAULTS[_pillar_flags.FLAG_AUTH]
22430 
22431     def _presented_token(self):
22432         """Any token the request carried (``?token=`` / Authorization / WS proto),
22433         or ``None`` — used only to record WHETHER a token was presented, never its
22434         value."""
22435         try:
22436             q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)
22437             provided = q.get("token", [None])[0]
22438             if provided is None:
22439                 provided = _paths.token_from_authorization(
22440                     self.headers.get("Authorization"))
22441             if provided is None:
22442                 provided = self.headers.get("Sec-WebSocket-Protocol")
22443             if provided is None:
22444                 # W9: the browser auth cookie is also a presented token.
22445                 provided = _paths.token_from_cookie(
22446                     self.headers.get("Cookie"))
22447             return provided
22448         except Exception:
22449             return None
22450 
22451     def _data_plane_gate(self, method, path):
22452         """Apply the W8/W9 auth-mode overlay to the reviewed data-plane batch.
22453 
22454         Returns True iff the request was HANDLED here (a 401 was sent) and the
22455         caller must ``return``. Behavior by mode for a route in
22456         ``route_table.DATA_PLANE_GATED``:
22457 
22458           * ``open`` (today)  → False (serve; no overlay).
22459           * ``warn`` (W8)     → for a TOKENLESS request, append a would-401 entry
22460             to the soak log, then return False (log-only — STILL served).
22461           * ``enforce`` (W9)  → for a TOKENLESS request, send 401 + return True.
22462 
22463         An authorized request (valid token) is always served (False) in every
22464         mode. A non-gated / unmatched route is a no-op (False).
22465         """
22466         route = _routes.match(method, path)
22467         if not _routes.is_data_plane_gated(route):
22468             return False
22469         mode = self._auth_mode()
22470         if mode == _auth_warn.MODE_OPEN:
22471             return False
22472         if self._term_token_ok():
22473             return False
22474         # Tokenless request against a gated route while warned/enforced.
22475         try:
22476             remote = None
22477             addr = getattr(self, "client_address", None)
22478             if addr:
22479                 remote = addr[0]
22480             _auth_warn.record_would_401(
22481                 method, path,
22482                 remote=remote,
22483                 has_token=self._presented_token() is not None,
22484                 user_agent=self.headers.get("User-Agent"),
22485                 referer=self.headers.get("Referer"),
22486                 mode=mode,
22487             )
22488         except Exception:
22489             # Logging must never break the request during the soak.
22490             pass
22491         if mode == _auth_warn.MODE_ENFORCE:
22492             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "unauthorized"}, 401)
22493             return True
22494         return False  # warn: observe-only, fall through to the legacy handler
22495 
22496     def _serve_term_stream2(self):
22497         """SSE-out fallback for a ConPTY session (Wave 3).
22498 
22499         The plan's named fallback half: an ``text/event-stream`` of a ConPTY
22500         session's output via ``pty_manager.read_since`` (through
22501         ``terminal_session.read_since``). Modeled on :meth:`_serve_term_sse` —
22502         bounded by ``max_ticks``, heartbeated, ends with a ``done`` event on a
22503         terminal (``dead``) status or when the tick budget elapses. Query knobs
22504         ``poll``/``max_ticks``/``hb``/``since`` mirror the v2 SSE handler.
22505 
22506         AUTH: ``?token=`` (401 when a token is configured and missing/wrong).
22507         """
22508         if not self._term_token_ok():
22509             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "unauthorized"}, 401)
22510             return
22511         q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)
22512         session = (q.get("session", [""])[0] or "").strip()
22513         try:
22514             since = int(q.get("since", ["0"])[0] or 0)
22515         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22516             since = 0
22517         if not session:
22518             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "missing session"}, 400)
22519             return
22520         try:
22521             poll_interval = float(q.get("poll", ["0.25"])[0] or 0.25)
22522         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22523             poll_interval = 0.25
22524         try:
22525             # High backstop (the loop ends on a terminal session or client
22526             # disconnect); the old 240/5000 ceiling froze the SSE fallback after
22527             # ~60s. Tests pass an explicit small max_ticks.
22528             max_ticks = int(q.get("max_ticks", ["4000000"])[0] or 4000000)
22529         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22530             max_ticks = 4000000
22531         # Clamp client-supplied knobs (self-DoS guard): poll in [0.01, 1.0]s,
22532         # max_ticks in [1, 4_000_000] (high backstop — loop ends on close/done).
22533         poll_interval = min(1.0, max(0.01, poll_interval))
22534         max_ticks = min(4000000, max(1, max_ticks))
22535         try:
22536             heartbeat_every = int(q.get("hb", ["8"])[0] or 8)
22537         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22538             heartbeat_every = 8
22539 
22540         self.send_response(200)
22541         self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream; charset=utf-8")
22542         self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache, no-store")
22543         self.send_header("Connection", "close")
22544         self.end_headers()
22545 
22546         cursor = since
22547         last_status = None
22548         idle = 0
22549         try:
22550             # ── attach-ack / replay-complete handshake (telemetry-resume W6) ──
22551             # The SSE fallback mirrors the WS attach-ack: a dead/unknown session
22552             # emits an explicit ``attach_ack ok:false`` event (the client paints
22553             # its error state) instead of a bare terminating stream; a live one
22554             # emits ``attach_ack ok:true`` + a ``replay_complete`` after the first
22555             # read, so the pane swaps in only once the buffer is replayed.
22556             try:
22557                 first = _termsess.read_since(session, cursor)
22558             except Exception:
22559                 first = {"ok": False, "reason": "error"}
22560             if not first.get("ok", True):
22561                 self._sse_event("attach_ack", {"ok": False,
22562                                                "reason": first.get(
22563                                                    "reason", "unknown-session")})
22564                 self._sse_event("done", {"status": "error",
22565                                          "next": cursor, "error": True})
22566                 return
22567             self._sse_event("attach_ack", {"ok": True})
22568             ftext = first.get("text", "")
22569             if ftext:
22570                 self._sse_event("output", {"text": ftext,
22571                                            "next": first.get("next", cursor)})
22572                 cursor = first.get("next", cursor)
22573             self._sse_event("replay_complete", {"next": cursor})
22574             for _tick in range(max(1, max_ticks)):
22575                 try:
22576                     out = _termsess.read_since(session, cursor)
22577                     if not out.get("ok", True):  # unknown session
22578                         self._sse_event("done", {"status": "error",
22579                                                  "next": cursor, "error": True})
22580                         return
22581                     text = out.get("text", "")
22582                     if text:
22583                         self._sse_event("output", {"text": text,
22584                                                    "next": out.get("next", cursor)})
22585                         cursor = out.get("next", cursor)
22586                         idle = 0
22587                     else:
22588                         idle += 1
22589                     status = out.get("status")
22590                     if status and status != last_status:
22591                         self._sse_event("status", {"status": status})
22592                         last_status = status
22593                     if status == "dead":
22594                         final = _termsess.read_since(session, cursor)
22595                         ft = final.get("text", "") if isinstance(final, dict) else ""
22596                         if ft:
22597                             self._sse_event("output", {"text": ft,
22598                                                        "next": final.get("next", cursor)})
22599                             cursor = final.get("next", cursor)
22600                         self._sse_event("done", {"status": status, "next": cursor})
22601                         return
22602                     if heartbeat_every and idle and idle % heartbeat_every == 0:
22603                         self._sse_event("heartbeat", {"next": cursor})
22604                 except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):
22605                     raise
22606                 except Exception:
22607                     try:
22608                         self._sse_event("done", {"status": "error",
22609                                                  "next": cursor, "error": True})
22610                     except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):
22611                         pass
22612                     return
22613                 time.sleep(max(0.0, poll_interval))
22614             self._sse_event("done", {"status": last_status or "running",
22615                                      "next": cursor, "bounded": True})
22616         except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):
22617             return
22618 
22619     def _serve_term_ws(self):
22620         """Hand-rolled stdlib WebSocket terminal endpoint (Wave 3, RFC 6455).
22621 
22622         Detects the ``Upgrade: websocket`` handshake, authenticates via
22623         ``?token=`` (or the ``Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`` header), computes the
22624         ``Sec-WebSocket-Accept`` value, replies ``101 Switching Protocols``, then
22625         takes over the raw socket and pumps PTY bytes BOTH ways:
22626 
22627         - decode client frames (text/binary -> ``terminal_session.input``;
22628           close -> end; ping -> pong);
22629         - poll ``terminal_session.read_since`` for new output -> encode + send
22630           server text frames.
22631 
22632         The pump loop is BOUNDED/interruptible (``poll``/``max_ticks`` query
22633         knobs, same as the SSE handler) so it ends cleanly on client close or a
22634         terminal (``dead``) session and is testable without hanging.
22635         """
22636         # AUTH FIRST: never upgrade an unauthorized handshake.
22637         if not self._term_token_ok():
22638             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "unauthorized"}, 401)
22639             return
22640 
22641         key = self.headers.get("Sec-WebSocket-Key")
22642         if not key:
22643             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "missing Sec-WebSocket-Key"},
22644                             400)
22645             return
22646 
22647         q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)
22648         session = (q.get("session", [""])[0] or "").strip()
22649         if not session:
22650             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "missing session"}, 400)
22651             return
22652         try:
22653             poll_interval = float(q.get("poll", ["0.05"])[0] or 0.05)
22654         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22655             poll_interval = 0.05
22656         try:
22657             # Default is effectively "for the life of the connection": the loop
22658             # already breaks on client close (recv b"") or a dead session, so this
22659             # is only a runaway backstop. The old 1200/5000 ceiling (~60-250s) was
22660             # the FREEZE bug — a multi-minute session lost its stream and went
22661             # silent. Tests pass an explicit small max_ticks via the query knob.
22662             max_ticks = int(q.get("max_ticks", ["4000000"])[0] or 4000000)
22663         except (TypeError, ValueError):
22664             max_ticks = 4000000
22665         # Clamp client-supplied knobs (self-DoS guard): poll in [0.01, 1.0]s,
22666         # max_ticks in [1, 4_000_000] (a high backstop — the loop ends on close).
22667         poll_interval = min(1.0, max(0.01, poll_interval))
22668         max_ticks = min(4000000, max(1, max_ticks))
22669 
22670         # ── 101 handshake ────────────────────────────────────────────────
22671         accept = ws_accept_key(key)
22672         handshake = (
22673             "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\n"
22674             "Upgrade: websocket\r\n"
22675             "Connection: Upgrade\r\n"
22676             "Sec-WebSocket-Accept: " + accept + "\r\n"
22677             "\r\n"
22678         )
22679         try:
22680             self.connection.sendall(handshake.encode("ascii"))
22681         except OSError:
22682             return
22683 
22684         # ── raw-socket pump (both ways), bounded + interruptible ─────────
22685         sock = self.connection
22686         sock.settimeout(max(0.01, poll_interval))
22687         inbuf = b""
22688         # CURSOR RESUME (2026-07-26 hardening, P0.1). This used to hard-code
22689         # ``cursor = 0``, so every WS (re)attach replayed the ENTIRE retained
22690         # 200KB PTY buffer on top of whatever the client already had on screen —
22691         # the terminal double-printing. The SSE path already honored ``since``;
22692         # the WS path had no knob at all. Same parse, same clamp, same default.
22693         try:
22694             _q = parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)
22695             cursor = int(_q.get("since", ["0"])[0] or 0)
22696             if cursor < 0:
22697                 cursor = 0
22698         except Exception:
22699             cursor = 0
22700         ws_state = {}  # persistent fragmentation-reassembly state for decode_frames
22701         try:
22702             # ── attach-ack / replay-complete handshake (telemetry-resume W6) ──
22703             # Resolve the session BEFORE the pump and send an explicit ack: a
22704             # dead/unknown session yields ``attach_ack ok:false`` (the client
22705             # paints its styled error state, narration still visible) rather than
22706             # the old SILENT break that wrote zero bytes → a blank pane (diag-B2
22707             # S1). A live session gets ``attach_ack ok:true``, its buffered output
22708             # is replayed, then ``replay_complete`` — the client swaps in the live
22709             # pane ONLY after that signal, so a blank pane is a protocol
22710             # impossibility.
22711             try:
22712                 first = _termsess.read_since(session, cursor)
22713             except Exception:
22714                 first = {"ok": False, "reason": "error"}
22715             if not first.get("ok", True):
22716                 try:
22717                     sock.sendall(ws_ctl_frame({
22718                         "type": "attach_ack", "ok": False,
22719                         "reason": first.get("reason", "unknown-session")}))
22720                 except OSError:
22721                     pass
22722                 return  # finally sends the close frame; client shows error state
22723             try:
22724                 sock.sendall(ws_ctl_frame({"type": "attach_ack", "ok": True,
22725                                            "session": session}))
22726                 replay = first.get("text", "")
22727                 if replay:
22728                     sock.sendall(encode_text_frame(replay))
22729                 cursor = first.get("next", cursor)
22730                 sock.sendall(ws_ctl_frame({"type": "replay_complete",
22731                                            "next": cursor}))
22732             except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):
22733                 return
22734             for _tick in range(max(1, max_ticks)):
22735                 # 1) Drain client -> PTY (non-blocking-ish via the socket timeout).
22736                 try:
22737                     chunk = sock.recv(65536)
22738                     if chunk == b"":
22739                         break  # client closed the TCP connection
22740                     inbuf += chunk
22741                     # Guard the carried inbuf so an endless stream of incomplete
22742                     # frame headers can't grow it without bound either.
22743                     if len(inbuf) > MAX_WS_FRAME:
22744                         break
22745                     msgs, inbuf = decode_frames(inbuf, ws_state,
22746                                                 require_mask=True)
22747                     closed = False
22748                     for opcode, payload in msgs:
22749                         if opcode in (WS_SIGNAL_CLOSE, WS_OP_CLOSE):
22750                             # Protocol error or a client close -> clean close.
22751                             closed = True
22752                             break
22753                         if opcode == WS_OP_PING:
22754                             try:
22755                                 sock.sendall(encode_pong_frame(payload))
22756                             except OSError:
22757                                 closed = True
22758                                 break
22759                             continue
22760                         if opcode == WS_OP_PONG:
22761                             continue  # unsolicited pong — ignore
22762                         if opcode in (WS_OP_TEXT, WS_OP_BINARY):
22763                             # Reassembled, complete data message (CONT frames are
22764                             # folded in by the codec — never delivered alone).
22765                             data = payload.decode("utf-8", "replace")
22766                             res = _termsess.input(session, data)
22767                             if not res.get("ok"):
22768                                 closed = True
22769                                 break
22770                     if closed:
22771                         break
22772                 except socket.timeout:
22773                     pass
22774                 except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):
22775                     break
22776 
22777                 # 2) Pump PTY -> client.
22778                 try:
22779                     out = _termsess.read_since(session, cursor)
22780                 except Exception:
22781                     break
22782                 if not out.get("ok", True):
22783                     break  # unknown session
22784                 text = out.get("text", "")
22785                 if text:
22786                     try:
22787                         sock.sendall(encode_text_frame(text))
22788                     except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):
22789                         break
22790                     cursor = out.get("next", cursor)
22791                 if out.get("status") == "dead":
22792                     # Drain any final output, then close cleanly.
22793                     final = _termsess.read_since(session, cursor)
22794                     ft = final.get("text", "") if isinstance(final, dict) else ""
22795                     if ft:
22796                         try:
22797                             sock.sendall(encode_text_frame(ft))
22798                         except OSError:
22799                             pass
22800                     break
22801         finally:
22802             try:
22803                 sock.sendall(encode_close_frame())
22804             except OSError:
22805                 pass

23461     def do_POST(self):
23462       try:
23463         content_len = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
23464         # Reject an oversized cockpit upload before reading/base64-decoding its
23465         # body. The route's decoded-file ceiling is 30 MB; 41 MB safely covers
23466         # base64 plus the small JSON envelope without buffering arbitrary data.
23467         if (urlparse(self.path).path == "/api/steward/upload"
23468                 and content_len > 41_000_000):
23469             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "over 30 MB"}, 413)
23470             return
23471         body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(content_len)) if content_len > 0 else {}
23472 
23473         # Contract-versioning shim (re-architecture 2026-07 · W2). A browser
23474         # page declares the build id it was rendered from (window.ANCHOR_BOOT
23475         # → the X-Anchor-Build header on every _postJson/apiCall). A mismatch
23476         # means the tab predates the current deploy (stale JS about to call a
23477         # migrated server): answer a STRUCTURED 409 the old client renders as
23478         # the 'reload required' banner — never an opaque failure. Consumers
23479         # that declare no build (healthcheck, CLI, curl) are never blocked.
23480         # Checked BEFORE auth so a stale tab learns 'reload' instead of
23481         # re-prompting for a token (the build id is already public via
23482         # GET /api/version — nothing new is leaked).
23483         client_build = (self.headers.get("X-Anchor-Build") or "").strip()
23484         if client_build and client_build != BUILD_ID:
23485             self._send_json({
23486                 "ok": False,
23487                 "error": BUILD_MISMATCH_ERROR,
23488                 "reason": "reload-required",
23489                 "server_build": BUILD_ID,
23490                 "client_build": client_build,
23491                 "action": "reload",
23492             }, 409)
23493             return
23494 
23495         # Token-auth middleware (Wave 2 / D4). Every mutating /api/* POST
23496         # requires a valid shared-secret token when ANCHOR_TOKEN is configured.
23497         # If ANCHOR_TOKEN is unset, auth is disabled (local-only back-compat).
23498         # The token may be supplied via the X-Anchor-Token header (preferred
23499         # by the browser clients), the standard Authorization header
23500         # (Bearer <token> or a bare token — the rearch-W2 path every
23501         # non-browser consumer uses), or a "token" field in the JSON body.
23502         # Read endpoints are not gated.
23503         # 2026-10-01 (Grok's independent review): ONE rule with the GET gate - any valid credential this POST carries
23504         # counts, the auth cookie included. Before, the first one seen was the only one judged, so a browser whose
23505         # SAVED token had gone stale sent it in X-Anchor-Token on every POST and was refused - the login after a
23506         # paste among them - while its reads rode a good cookie, and the box stayed.
23507         _cands = [self.headers.get("X-Anchor-Token"),
23508                   _paths.token_from_authorization(self.headers.get("Authorization")),
23509                   body.get("token") if isinstance(body, dict) else None,
23510                   _paths.token_from_cookie(self.headers.get("Cookie"))]
23511         _cands = [t for t in _cands if t]
23512         provided = next((t for t in _cands if _paths.auth_ok(t)), _cands[0] if _cands else None)
23513         # Default-deny by construction, driven by the declared route table (W7):
23514         # a POST is gated UNLESS its row explicitly declares ``auth == open``. No
23515         # POST is open today, so behavior is unchanged — but the middleware now
23516         # DEFERS to the reviewed table (+ OPEN_ROUTES) instead of blanket-gating,
23517         # so an undeclared POST is still default-denied while a future reviewed
23518         # open POST would be honored (rearch W8: post-middleware consults the
23519         # route-table auth policy).
23520         _path_only = urlparse(self.path).path
23521         _post_route = _routes.match("POST", _path_only)
23522         _post_open = (_post_route is not None
23523                       and _post_route.auth == _routes.AUTH_OPEN)
23524         if not _post_open and not _paths.auth_ok(provided):
23525             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "unauthorized"}, 401)
23526             return
23527 
23528         # --- Steward cockpit POST (additive; token-gated by the check above) ---
23529         if _path_only.startswith("/api/steward/"):
23530             self._steward_api("POST", _path_only[len("/api/steward/"):], body)
23531             return
23532 
23533         # Auth-cookie bootstrap (steward-chamber W11). The login/logout mint
23534         # is part of the AUTH MIDDLEWARE layer, not the dispatch surface: it
23535         # runs here — after the token check above, before the strangler seam —
23536         # so a post-auth dispatch shim (the chamber F6 harness swaps
23537         # _strangler_dispatch for a marker responder) can never swallow the
23538         # Set-Cookie handshake. The rows stay declared/migrated in
23539         # route_table.py and _strangler_dispatch still resolves them when
23540         # called directly.
23541         if _path_only == "/api/auth/login":
23542             handle_auth_login(self, self.path, body)
23543             return
23544         if _path_only == "/api/auth/logout":
23545             handle_auth_logout(self, self.path, body)
23546             return
23547 
23548         # Strangler dispatch (rearch W7 / C2): consult the declarative route
23549         # table FIRST. Runs AFTER the token middleware, so a migrated POST row is
23550         # already authenticated. Unmatched / not-yet-migrated POSTs fall through
23551         # to the legacy if/elif chain below unchanged.
23552         #
23553         # (2026-07-30 FIX) Dispatch on the PATH-ONLY string, exactly like the
23554         # auth lookup two lines up (and like do_GET, which already passes
23555         # ``_path_only``). ``_routes.match`` compares an EXACT row with ``path ==
23556         # pattern``, so passing the raw request line meant ANY POST carrying a
23557         # query string missed its exact row, fell through the strangler, and
23558         # answered 404 "Unknown endpoint". That is what broke every steward act
23559         # (/api/ecgberht/stand_up?token=… → "Couldn't do that: Unknown
23560         # endpoint"): the URLs carry ?token=, so with auth ON they could never
23561         # dispatch — and with auth OFF the query is empty, which is why the
23562         # suites never saw it. Handlers still receive the FULL URI (query
23563         # included) — _strangler_dispatch passes ``self.path`` to the handler.
23564         if self._strangler_dispatch("POST", _path_only, body):
23565             return
23566             
23567         # /api/doctor/run removed (doctor V3 wave 1). The V2 handler spawned a
23568         # third-party Gemini API-key wrapper script (deleted; stdlib-only
23569         # violation, unusable on a subscription-CLI host) and ran
23570         # anchor_healthcheck.py synchronously in the request thread for up to
23571         # 75s. V3 replaces them with a real agentic session on the existing PTY
23572         # substrate (wave 2) and a background healthcheck run with a live tail
23573         # (wave 3). An unmatched POST here falls through to the 404 below.
23574 
23575         # /api/rnd/upload_batch migrated to route_table (handle_upload_batch) — served by the strangler above.
23576         # /api/upload migrated to route_table (handle_upload) — served by the strangler above.
23577         # /api/rnd/reaper_arm, /api/rnd/reaper_advance, /api/rnd/reaper_disarm
23578         # migrated to route_table — served by the strangler above.
23579         # 2026-05-12: /api/shutdown removed. The NSSM "anchor" service owns
23580         # process lifecycle; the dashboard cannot kill the server.
23581         # Any POST not handled by the strangler above is an unknown endpoint.
23582         self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": "Unknown endpoint"}, 404)
23583       except Exception as e:
23584             if _is_benign_disconnect(e):
23585                 # Client closed the connection mid-POST. Not a server error.
23586                 return
23587             _logger.error(f"POST {self.path} failed: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}")
23588             self._send_json({"ok": False, "error": str(e)}, 500)

23596 def _heartbeat_watchdog():
23597     """Background thread: heartbeat monitoring disabled.
23598 
23599     The server now runs until explicitly stopped — via the Stop button in the
23600     dashboard, Ctrl+C in the terminal, or by killing the Python process. This
23601     keeps the dashboard instantly available when the user comes back to the
23602     tab after any amount of time.

23607 class _QuietDisconnectMixin:
23608     """Server mixin that quiets BENIGN client-disconnect errors.
23609 
23610     socketserver calls ``handle_error(request, client_address)`` when a request
23611     handler raises an unhandled exception, and by default it prints a full
23612     traceback to stderr. A browser closing a terminal tab (or Playwright tearing
23613     a page down) makes an in-flight SSE/WS/HTTP write raise
23614     ``ConnectionAbortedError``/``ConnectionResetError``/``BrokenPipeError`` (on
23615     Windows often a bare ``OSError`` with ``winerror`` 10053/10054). That is the
23616     client going away, not a server bug — so we swallow it silently here as a
23617     last line of defense (the handlers already break out of their stream loops
23618     on these). Any OTHER exception still gets the normal noisy traceback so real
23619     defects are never hidden.
23620     """
23621 
23622     # Accept backlog (``listen(N)``). socketserver's default is 5 — and Windows
23623     # answers the 6th pending connection with RST (WinError 10061 "actively
23624     # refused") whenever the accept loop lags a burst: a browser opening 6+
23625     # parallel asset/SSE/WS connections behind a GIL-heavy render. 64 keeps a
23626     # burst queued for the accept loop instead of refusing it.
23627     request_queue_size = 64
23628 
23629     def handle_error(self, request, client_address):
23630         exc = sys.exc_info()[1]
23631         if _is_benign_disconnect(exc):
23632             return
23633         super().handle_error(request, client_address)

23636 class _ExclusiveThreadingHTTPServer(_QuietDisconnectMixin, ThreadingHTTPServer):
23637     """ThreadingHTTPServer that claims EXCLUSIVE ownership of its port.
23638 
23639     On Windows, ``socket.SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE`` guarantees only ONE process can
23640     own the listening port — so a duplicate/orphan Anchor process can never
23641     silently squat 8777 and serve stale code. We deliberately turn OFF
23642     ``allow_reuse_address`` (HTTPServer enables SO_REUSEADDR by default, which
23643     is what permits port sharing) and set SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE before binding.
23644 
23645     Used ONLY for the real fixed-port path (see ``make_server``). The ephemeral
23646     ``port=0`` path used by the tests/health check keeps the default behavior.
23647     """
23648 
23649     # HTTPServer sets this to 1 (SO_REUSEADDR). Force it off for exclusivity.
23650     allow_reuse_address = False
23651 
23652     def server_bind(self):
23653         try:
23654             self.socket.setsockopt(
23655                 socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE, 1
23656             )
23657         except (AttributeError, OSError):
23658             # SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE is Windows-only; on any platform/socket that
23659             # rejects it, fall back to the default bind (use_exclusive_bind
23660             # already gates us to Windows, so this is just belt-and-suspenders).
23661             pass
23662         super().server_bind()
23663 
23664 
23665 class _PosixExclusiveThreadingHTTPServer(_QuietDisconnectMixin, ThreadingHTTPServer):
23666     """ThreadingHTTPServer that claims single-ownership of its port on POSIX.
23667 
23668     share-distro v1 Wave 2 (MASTER-PLAN decision #6 — POSIX single-instance
23669     guard). macOS/Linux have no ``SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE``; instead the guard simply
23670     leaves ``SO_REUSEADDR`` **OFF** (``allow_reuse_address = False``) for the real
23671     fixed port. A second Anchor binding the same port then fails with
23672     ``EADDRINUSE`` — which ``paths.classify_bind_error`` maps to a clean
23673     ``exit(0)`` in ``main`` (exactly the Windows ``SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE`` parity:
23674     one mechanism, no pidfile). Used ONLY for the real fixed-port path on
23675     non-Windows (see ``make_server``); the ephemeral ``port=0`` path is unaffected.
23676     """
23677 
23678     # HTTPServer sets this to 1 (SO_REUSEADDR). Force it off so a duplicate bind
23679     # on the same fixed port raises EADDRINUSE instead of silently sharing it.
23680     allow_reuse_address = False
23681 
23682 
23683 class _QuietThreadingHTTPServer(_QuietDisconnectMixin, ThreadingHTTPServer):
23684     """Plain ThreadingHTTPServer for the ephemeral ``port=0`` path (tests /
23685     health check) that also quiets benign client-disconnect errors — so a
23686     Playwright teardown racing an in-flight stream can't print a traceback or
23687     flake the gate."""
23688     daemon_threads = True
23689 
23690 
23691 def make_server(host="127.0.0.1", port=8777, activate=True):
23692     """Construct + bind the threading HTTP server.
23693 
23694     ``activate=False`` BINDS the port — so the single-instance guard below
23695     fires exactly as before (a duplicate's bind still fails) — but does NOT
23696     ``listen()`` yet. The caller runs its boot work, then calls
23697     ``server.server_activate()`` right before ``serve_forever()``. Until then a
23698     client's connect is never accepted or queued — POSIX refuses it, Windows
23699     drops the SYN to a bound-but-unlistened port — instead of sitting in a
23700     backlog nobody is draining, so "the port accepts connections" means "the
23701     server is serving". ``main()`` uses this; tests / the health check keep the
23702     default bind+listen construction.
23703 
23704     Two distinct bind-failure modes are reconciled here (D4/Wave 2 + Wave 3
23705     single-instance guard):
23706 
23707     - **Transient** failures (e.g. EADDRNOTAVAIL — a slow-to-come-up Tailscale
23708       interface not yet assignable) are retried by ``paths.bind_with_retry``.
23709     - **Address already owned by another Anchor** (EADDRINUSE) is NOT retried —
23710       ``bind_with_retry`` re-raises it immediately so the caller can exit
23711       cleanly instead of spinning into a bad state.
23712 
23713     For the real fixed port (non-zero, on Windows) we bind with
23714     SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE so the OS guarantees a single owner. The ``port=0``
23715     ephemeral path (tests / health check) keeps the default ThreadingHTTPServer
23716     behavior so OS-assigned ports are unaffected.
23717     """
23718     if _paths.use_exclusive_bind(host, port):
23719         # Windows real fixed port → SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE single-owner guard.
23720         server_cls = _ExclusiveThreadingHTTPServer
23721     elif _paths.use_posix_exclusive_bind(host, port):
23722         # POSIX real fixed port → SO_REUSEADDR OFF so a duplicate bind raises
23723         # EADDRINUSE → classify_bind_error → clean exit(0) (Wave-2 parity).
23724         server_cls = _PosixExclusiveThreadingHTTPServer
23725     else:
23726         # Ephemeral port=0 (tests / health check) → unchanged default behavior.
23727         server_cls = _QuietThreadingHTTPServer
23728     if not activate:
23729         def _bind_only():
23730             # Mirror socketserver's own constructor: bind, and on ANY failure
23731             # release the socket before re-raising (bind_with_retry classifies
23732             # the OSError — EADDRINUSE → the clean single-instance exit).
23733             srv = server_cls((host, port), AnchorHandler, bind_and_activate=False)
23734             try:
23735                 srv.server_bind()
23736             except BaseException:
23737                 srv.server_close()
23738                 raise
23739             return srv
23740         return _paths.bind_with_retry(_bind_only)
23741     return _paths.bind_with_retry(
23742         lambda: server_cls((host, port), AnchorHandler)
23743     )
23744 
23745 
23746 _LOOPBACK_HOSTS = ("127.0.0.1", "::1", "localhost")
23747 
23748 
23749 def resolve_bind_host():
23750     """Resolve the server bind host from ``ANCHOR_BIND`` (default loopback).
23751 
23752     Set ``ANCHOR_BIND`` to the Tailscale IP (e.g. ``100.69.215.4``) to expose the
23753     dashboard over the tailnet. SAFETY (D4): refuse a non-loopback bind unless
23754     ``ANCHOR_TOKEN`` is configured — otherwise every mutating ``/api/*`` endpoint
23755     (including the ``bypassPermissions`` build lane) would be reachable
23756     unauthenticated. Returns the host string; raises ``RuntimeError`` for the
23757     unsafe combination so ``main`` can refuse to start.
23758     """
23759     host = (os.environ.get("ANCHOR_BIND") or "127.0.0.1").strip() or "127.0.0.1"
23760     if host not in _LOOPBACK_HOSTS and _paths.expected_token() is None:
23761         raise RuntimeError(
23762             f"Refusing to bind {host} without ANCHOR_TOKEN set — that would "
23763             f"expose mutating endpoints (incl. the build lane) unauthenticated. "
23764             f"Set ANCHOR_TOKEN, or use ANCHOR_BIND=127.0.0.1 for local-only."
23765         )
23766     return host

23904         # immutable snapshot/provider the banner + daemon use (reaper.live_pid_ids

24046             # default. Each cycle does ONE running-record read and builds the ONE
24047             # immutable snapshot (the single shared provider — same source the
24048             # banner/view/brief/boot-reconcile sites use), derives the live-owner
24049             # set from THAT snapshot (abstain-safe), caches it for _live_provider,
24050             # then routes the SAME snapshot + records through
24051             # reaper_arming.armed_sweep, whose effective tier (log → freeze → kill)
24052             # honors the persisted arm state AND the restart-durable
24053             # .anchor/reaper.disarmed kill-switch brake. Every destructive action
24054             # is re-derived in-process from the fresh snapshot (protect-only) — a
24055             # persisted 'kill' tier never kills a session whose owner is alive. A
24056             # second build_snapshot here would violate the single-source contract.
24057             import reaper_arming
24058             _daemon_owners = {"set": set()}
24059             def _live_provider():
24060                 # The daemon's live-owner set, derived from the most-recent sweep
24061                 # snapshot (abstain-safe PTY-attached fallback before the first
24062                 # sweep). Never builds a second snapshot.
24063                 return _daemon_owners["set"] or set(pty_manager._LIVE.keys())
24064             def _armed_sweep_cycle():
24065                 try:
24066                     running = _sr_daemon.list_sessions(status="running")
24067                 except Exception:
24068                     running = []
24069                 attached = set(pty_manager._LIVE.keys())
24070                 try:
24071                     snap = reaper.build_snapshot(attached_pty_ids=attached,
24072                                                  records=running,
24073                                                  enumerate_pids=reaper.enumerate_live_pids)
24074                 except Exception:
24075                     snap = None
24076                 # Derive the live-owner set DIRECTLY from the one snapshot via the
24077                 # shared provider. Defensive boundary (Wave 2, criterion 1): a
24078                 # degraded/None snapshot → owner_ids_or_abstain returns EVERY
24079                 # running id as "owned", so a single fetch hiccup can never feed
24080                 # the armed daemon a narrowed live set → mass-kill.
24081                 try:
24082                     if snap is not None and not getattr(snap, "degraded", False):
24083                         _daemon_owners["set"] = reaper.live_owner_ids(snap) or attached
24084                     else:
24085                         _daemon_owners["set"] = (
24086                             reaper.owner_ids_or_abstain(snap, running) or attached)
24087                 except Exception:
24088                     _daemon_owners["set"] = attached
24089                 reaper_arming.armed_sweep(running, snap)
24090             zombie_hunter.start_hunter(_live_provider, sweep_fn=_armed_sweep_cycle)
24091

24094                 # _ensure_zh_node_server if the user opens the radar before listen.
24095                 import subprocess as _sp_zh
24096                 if not _zh_node_is_up(timeout=0.5):
24097                     creationflags = 0x08000000 if sys.platform.startswith("win") else 0
24098                     if os.path.exists(_ZH_NODE_SERVER_PATH):
